rounds.observation: Only 2 of 20 evaluated designs are feasible, and 11 of the 20 returned no geometry. All 11 geometry failures fit one rule I derived from the reported negative cone lengths: fore-cone length = (y2 - y1)/tan(theta), where y1 = Rn*cos(theta) with Rn = bluntness*D, y2 = D/2 - Rs*(1 - cos(theta)) with Rs = 0.1*D. It reproduces -81 mm (C-8fe9c875d634), -367 mm (C-892b8b20e709) and -5413 mm (C-c9569b91ff83). The rule reduces to (bluntness - 0.1)*cos(theta) <= 0.4, independent of D. I hold every proposal to <= 0.376 for margin. The other constraint limits are max_g <= 12 g, bondline <= 450 K, and a mass-fraction limit that scales roughly as D^2 (D up to about 3.3 m). Hypervolume is dominated by the bondline-temperature axis (a 150 K span versus 2.5 MW/m2 for flux). The current front is a single point, C-ca305253716b (345 kW/m2, 406.6 K). Rough log-fits to 9 metric rows suggest that a larger nose radius (bluntness*D) and larger D lower flux and bondline temperature. They also suggest that steeper entry lowers bondline temperature and raises g, with the g limit near gamma of -3.6 deg.
evidence: Geometry failures C-892b8b20e709, C-c170e00795a8, C-2fe8ade3b390 and C-8fe9c875d634 all violate (b-0.1)cos(theta) <= 0.4; valid rows C-ca305253716b (0.366), C-30ab3c9fdbef (0.361) and C-7e930f570744 (0.20) satisfy it.

g rises with steepness: C-30ab3c9fdbef -2.32 deg gives 9.85 g, C-ca305253716b -3.16 deg gives 11.2 g, C-7e930f570744 -4.54 deg gives 13.57 g. Steeper rows C-1d847642b793 and C-0a0993b4b67b give 16.6 and 18.8 g. The 12 g limit is therefore near -3.6 deg for large D.
Mass-fraction margin tracks D^2: C-ca305253716b (D 3.01) 0.185, C-0a0993b4b67b (D 3.74) -0.37, C-1d847642b793 (D 4.33) -0.77. Feasible D is at most about 3.3 m.
Low bondline temperature comes from large D and steep gamma: C-1d847642b793 372 K and C-0a0993b4b67b 374 K, versus small-D rows C-6c8d751b6b54 510 K and C-7139ecfe995b 469 K.
Shallow entry raises bondline temperature at similar flux: C-30ab3c9fdbef has 431.6 K at gamma -2.32 deg, versus 406.6 K for C-ca305253716b at -3.16 deg.
Normalised hypervolume 0.2496 equals (1-345120/2.5e6)*(450-406.56)/150, so the score depends heavily on the bondline term.
rounds.mechanism: Peak stagnation heating falls with nose radius (about 1/sqrt(Rn)) and with lower ballistic coefficient, i.e. larger D. Bondline temperature follows the heat load, so it falls with a shorter, steeper pulse and with lower peak flux. Steeper entry raises g. The mass fraction limits D to about 3.3 m and g limits gamma to about -3.6 deg. The best corner is therefore D near 3.2-3.3 m, the largest nose radius the geometry rule allows (bluntness about 1.1-1.2 with cone angle 68-70 deg), and gamma near -3.4 to -3.55 deg. Shallower gamma gives lower flux but higher bondline temperature, which traces the trade-off front.
rounds.uncertainty: The geometry rule is fitted to 11 failures plus valid rows, and I have not seen valid rows with bluntness above 0.88 at cone angles near 70 deg. The flux and bondline scalings come from about 9 rows with noisy exponents. I am relying on ballistic-entry scaling from prior knowledge for the sign and size of some trends. The effects of cone angle on g and drag, and the exact mass-fraction limit near D 3.3 m, are poorly constrained. The g boundary near gamma of -3.6 deg is interpolated.

rounds.observation: No feasible design exists yet. 10 of 20 evaluations failed on geometry and none of the 10 valid ones is feasible. The geometry failures fit a closed-form rule: the fore-cone length is (R - Rs(1-cos t) - Rn cos t)/tan t, with Rn = bluntness*D and Rs = 0.1*D. This is equivalent to (bluntness - 0.1)*cos(cone_half_angle) <= 0.4, independent of D. I reproduced the reported negative lengths of -48.9 mm (C-0e7ec9742f84) and -22.8 mm (C-2e989122c857), and it separates every valid row from every invalid row. I keep this quantity <= ~0.38 in every proposal. The limits implied by the margins are max_g 12.0 and bondline 450 K. Heatshield mass fraction scales roughly as 0.09*D^2 in units of its limit, which puts D at about 3.3 or below. Max_g is mainly set by flight-path angle, so gamma should be about -3.0 to -3.8 deg. On the valid points, flux falls with larger D and larger bluntness, and bondline temperature falls with larger D, steeper gamma and larger bluntness. So I target D ~3.0-3.3, high bluntness, cone angle 60-70 deg and gamma ~-3.5 deg.
evidence: Geometry rule check: C-cf5ade290acc (b=1.076, cone 33.9) gives 0.98*0.83=0.81 > 0.4, invalid. C-63aaa0985529 (b=0.523, cone 29.7) gives 0.37 <= 0.4, valid. C-7fd3f4505944 (0.65*0.80=0.52) is invalid and C-f97dae207371 (0.26) is valid. All 20 rows are consistent.
Max_g limit is 12.0: C-50a0a474d0f6 has 12.059 with margin -0.0049. The limit for bondline temperature is 450 K, from C-ee99f55de428 (455.54 with margin -0.0123).

Max_g vs gamma: 9.4 g at -1.85 (C-f97dae207371), 10.2 g at -2.64 (C-ee99f55de428), 12.5 g at -4.10 (C-63aaa0985529), 13.1 g at -4.26 (C-ab9827dc6929), 16.2-17.2 g at about -6 (C-baa2f9e65f32, C-26bc5a06b4e4, C-12010dd082dd). Small D looks slightly worse: C-50a0a474d0f6 reaches 12.06 g at only -3.1 deg. I therefore stay at gamma >= -3.9.

Mass fraction divided by D^2 is about 0.089-0.091 for cone >= 62 (C-36f9165b9496, C-baa2f9e65f32, C-c72c38c9187a, C-12010dd082dd), 0.097-0.101 for cone 42-53, and 0.11 for cone 30-38 (C-63aaa0985529, C-f97dae207371). The margin is 0.028 at D=2.985 with cone 29.7 and -0.004 at D=3.21 with cone 52.8, so high cone angle allows a larger D.

Bondline temperature fit on the valid rows: T-300 ~ 103*(D/3.21)^-0.8*(sin|gamma|/0.0743)^-0.4*(b/0.399)^-0.2, anchored on C-ab9827dc6929. It reproduces C-f97dae207371 (444.7), C-36f9165b9496 (398), C-26bc5a06b4e4 (373) and C-baa2f9e65f32 (373.6) to within a few K.

Flux fit anchored on C-ab9827dc6929 (479 kW/m2): q ~ 479k*(D/3.21)^-1.5*(b/0.399)^-0.5*(sin|gamma|/0.0743)^0.3. It matches C-26bc5a06b4e4, C-baa2f9e65f32 and C-c72c38c9187a within ~10%. C-63aaa0985529 (cone 29.7) is ~15% above the fit, which suggests small cone angles raise flux.

C-36f9165b9496 (b=0.87, cone 65) has the lowest bondline temperature of the mid-size designs (398 K at D=2.55) and fails only max_g (gamma -4.86). Raising D to ~3.1 and easing gamma to ~-3.6 should make it feasible.
rounds.mechanism: Peak heating falls as ballistic coefficient falls (larger D, higher drag from a blunter and wider cone) and as nose radius grows. Bondline temperature follows the integrated heat load, which is lower for steeper entry and higher for shallow entry, where the soak time is long. Peak deceleration is set mainly by entry angle, so shallow gamma protects max_g but raises bondline temperature. The best compromise is the largest D the mass-fraction limit allows, high bluntness with a cone wide enough to keep the geometry valid, and gamma of about -3.5 deg. High cone angle also reduces heatshield area, which buys diameter.
rounds.uncertainty: The scalings are my own fits to only 10 valid points, plus a physics prior for exponents. The bluntness effect beyond b=0.87 is extrapolated, since no valid point has b above 0.87. The g dependence on D and cone is poorly constrained. The mass-fraction limit near D=3.3 rests on a ~0.089*D^2 fit. The flux dependence on cone angle is only hinted at by C-63aaa0985529.

rounds.observation: No feasible design exists yet: 11 of 20 evaluations were geometry failures, and the rest fail max_g (limit 12 g), heatshield mass fraction, or both. All 11 geometry failures fit one rule: fore-cone length = D*(0.5 - 0.1*(1-cos(theta)) - b*cos(theta))/tan(theta), which must be >= 0. This reproduces the reported lengths for C-d03a6d571826, C-e0d635fd334b and C-c28d2aecc04e, so high bluntness needs a high cone angle. The feasible window looks like: flight-path angle no steeper than about -3.3 deg (g <= 12), diameter no larger than about 3.0 m (mass fraction), and a high cone angle with the largest bluntness the geometry allows. The hypervolume reference is 450 K in temperature, so bondline temperature dominates the hypervolume: one Kelvin is worth far more than tens of kW/m2 of heat flux. The proposals therefore cluster near the g and mass limits, with a few shallower or smaller probes for trade-off coverage.
evidence: C-e0059024652c: gamma -2.69 gives g 10.56 (margin 0.1201, so the g limit is 12). C-316c5e108e1a: gamma -3.40 gives g 11.97 (margin 0.002). Steeper entries fail g: C-9b459669aa7c gives 12.9 at -3.52 and C-029296252ff3 gives 13.6 at -4.41.

Mass-fraction margin falls with diameter: C-a6b969cef0a0 at D 3.07 gives +0.008, C-e0059024652c at 3.39 gives -0.128, C-029296252ff3 at 3.63 gives -0.19, C-316c5e108e1a at 4.30 gives -0.83. Small diameters pass easily, for example 0.83 at D 1.24 in C-9b459669aa7c. The diameter ceiling is therefore about 3.0 m.

Peak heat flux q roughly follows q^2 = K*sin(gamma)/(b*D^3), with K about 5e13 at theta 42-49 and about 3.2-3.6e13 at theta 55-65, fitted across the 9 valid rows. Higher cone angle, larger D and larger bluntness therefore all lower q and the heat load.

Bondline temperature rises with heat-load proxy Q = q/sin(gamma), roughly dT = 76 + 3.9*Q[MW/m2]. Examples: C-316c5e108e1a has Q 4.8 and T 393; C-9b459669aa7c has Q 28 and T 484. Shallow entry adds a few K (C-e0059024652c is about +9 K above trend at -2.69 deg).
Geometry-failure rows C-c28d2aecc04e, C-69ef29176b15 and C-5a78f6504d22 all combine bluntness above 0.96 with theta at or below 53 deg. Valid rows with b*cos(theta) below about 0.48 all built.
rounds.mechanism: Peak heating scales roughly with sqrt(rho/Rn)*V^3 (Sutton-Graves, prior knowledge). It falls with larger nose radius (Rn = b*D) and with lower ballistic coefficient (larger D and higher-drag blunt, high-angle cones). Bondline temperature follows integrated heat load, which falls with the same levers and rises as the entry gets shallower and the heating pulse lengthens. Peak deceleration is set mainly by entry angle, plus a small bump for small, high-ballistic-coefficient bodies. The best region is therefore large D within the mass limit, theta 62-70 deg, b near the geometry ceiling b <= (0.4 - margin)/cos(theta) + 0.1, and gamma near -3.1 to -3.3 deg. Shallower gamma trades higher T for lower q.
rounds.uncertainty: Diameter and gamma are extrapolated: the mass-fraction dependence on theta and b is unmeasured, and the 3.0 m ceiling comes from only three rows. g for large-D, high-drag blunt shapes at gamma -3.2 to -3.4 sits within about 0.4 g of the limit, so several proposals may fail g. K(theta) and the T-vs-Q fit come from 9 points with confounded variables. Predicted temperatures below 393 K are extrapolation. The 0.02-0.09 geometry margins are computed from the fitted rule and should be safe, but a minimum cone length may exist that the data does not show.

rounds.observation: Every feasible point sits at large D (about 3.2-3.3 m), high bluntness (1.1-1.18), cone angle near 70 deg and gamma between -2.2 and -3.5 deg. The hypervolume is 0.331. In normalised terms, 1 K of bondline temperature is worth about 0.6% of hypervolume, while 10k W/m2 of flux is worth only about 0.15%. Lowering bondline temperature therefore matters most. Two constraints bound the corner. max_g caps gamma at about -3.6 deg (limit about 12 g, roughly 1.6 g per degree, almost independent of D, bluntness and cone). The heatshield mass fraction caps D. Its margin scales roughly with D^2, and my extrapolation puts the limit near D = 3.38-3.40 m. The unexplored gains are a larger D, bluntness up to 1.35, and a spread of gamma values along the front.
evidence: D sweep at gamma -3.4 and bluntness 1.1: C-897b67e590d7 (D 2.9) gives 344k W/m2 and 403.0 K, C-5e1c13074d20 (D 3.2) gives 298.7k and 396.9 K, and C-84c7c9af373d (D 3.3) gives 285.8k and 395.0 K. Larger D lowers both objectives.

Mass-fraction margin versus D: 0.263 at 2.9 m (C-897b67e590d7), 0.103 at 3.2 (C-5e1c13074d20), 0.0748 at 3.25 (C-26ce9aa66580), 0.0455 at 3.3 (C-84c7c9af373d). The margin follows a D^2 scaling and would reach zero near 3.38 m. Bluntness 1.18 with cone 70 adds about +0.003 (C-15f0016ca61b, C-51e48573fc56).

Gamma sweep at D 3.2, bluntness 1.1, cone 69: gamma -3.25, -3.4, -3.55 and -3.7 give g 11.40, 11.64, 11.89 and 12.14, and bondline temperature 398.5, 396.9, 395.3 and 393.8 K. C-114b79b08144 (gamma -3.7) violates max_g at 12.136 g.

g depends almost only on gamma. C-7e930f570744 (gamma -4.54) gives 13.57 g and C-0a0993b4b67b (gamma -7.07) gives 18.8 g, while D and bluntness change g by only about 0.4 g per metre. Steeper entry cannot be bought back through geometry.

Bluntness 1.0 (cone 66), 1.1 (cone 69) and 1.18 (cone 70) at D 3.2, gamma -3.4 give 305.1k, 298.7k and 294.4k W/m2 and 397.7, 396.9 and 396.3 K (C-b6ef7565262e, C-5e1c13074d20, C-15f0016ca61b). Higher bluntness helps both objectives, and the mass margin does not degrade.

Shallow-gamma front points C-b86d67fded52 (gamma -2.2: 263.6k, 411.2 K) and C-a2a24d2b0ad2 (gamma -2.6: 277.6k, 406.3 K) show the flux versus temperature trade-off. A larger D and higher bluntness should shift this curve down and left.

All 8 geometry failures have a small cone angle relative to bluntness. From the reported negative cone lengths I fit a rough overlap condition, cos(theta)*(about 1.86*b - 0.1) < 0.9. Cone 70 with b up to 1.35 gives about 0.82-0.85, so it should be buildable. Cone 69 with b 1.3 gives about 0.83-0.86, also inside the limit. C-15f0016ca61b (b 1.18, cone 70) and C-51e48573fc56 already built.
rounds.mechanism: Stagnation heating falls with nose radius and with lower ballistic coefficient (larger D and bluntness). Peak bondline temperature follows the heat load, which is lower for a shorter, steeper pulse. Peak g is set almost entirely by gamma, since g_max is roughly independent of ballistic coefficient. The best corner is therefore the largest D the mass fraction allows (about 3.36-3.38 m), the largest bluntness the geometry allows (1.35 at cone 70), and gamma near the g limit (about -3.5 to -3.55 deg). Sweeping gamma from -1.8 to -3.4 at that D and bluntness fills the flux versus temperature front with points below the current one.
rounds.uncertainty: The extrapolation to b 1.35 is outside the sampled range, and the effect of bluntness on mass fraction there is unknown. The mass-fraction edge near D 3.38 is uncertain by about ±0.01 in margin. The g margin at gamma -3.55 is only about 0.5-1%. The geometry-overlap fit uses only 8 failures and could be wrong near b 1.35. I extrapolated the flux D-exponent of about -1.35 from a few points. All predicted values come from local linear extrapolation of the data shown, not from a validated model.

rounds.observation: Only 3 of 20 evaluated designs are feasible and 12 return no geometry. Every geometry failure has high bluntness_ratio combined with low cone_half_angle. Every valid geometry satisfies roughly (2*b - 0.1)*cos(theta) <= 0.86, and every failure is at or above 1.0. This is my own inference from the ids and the failure messages, not a stated rule. Feasible max_g is capped at 12 (C-1a25df448e6f sits at 11.99), and g rises with steeper flight_path_angle. Heat-shield mass fraction is roughly 1 - m ~ 0.09*D^2, so diameter must stay at or below about 3.2 m (C-c97855c2d790 at 4.27 m fails). The hypervolume is dominated by lowering bondline temperature, since the 300-450 K range is small. The current front point C-924ebfff660f is at 422 K and 363 kW/m2. Bluntness, diameter and flight-path angle are the levers still unexplored.
evidence: C-924ebfff660f (D=2.81, b=0.72, theta=69.6, gamma=-2.43) is the only front point: q=362.8k, T=422.0, g=10.1.

C-954afbe3d7da (b=0.396, theta=66.3, gamma=-1.79) has T=443 and q=418k. It is dominated by C-924ebfff660f, which has larger bluntness and a steeper angle, so higher bluntness and steeper entry lower T.

C-1a25df448e6f (gamma=-3.88, theta=36.4, D=2.39) sits at g=11.99, essentially on the g limit. Steeper angles (C-02335773e828 at -6.0 gives g=15.9, C-2d91d8d713d7 at -7.4 gives g=19.2) are clearly infeasible.

Steep, big-D designs reach low T but violate g: C-c97855c2d790 gives T=375, C-2d91d8d713d7 gives T=381 and C-02335773e828 gives T=394. Bondline temperature falls with a larger b*D^3*sin(gamma) product.

Geometry failures: C-1fdb98d93248 (b=1.32, theta=63.9), C-0c229251fec4 (b=1.26, theta=59.1), C-f97de340f655 (b=0.79, theta=47). Valid: C-c76d29c9a126 (b=0.515, theta=22.8) and C-924ebfff660f (b=0.72, theta=69.6). Large theta allows larger b.
rounds.mechanism: This relies on prior Allen-Eggers-type scaling, calibrated to the data. Peak stagnation heat flux scales as sqrt(sin(gamma)/(Rn*CdA)), so it falls with larger nose radius and larger diameter. Heat load, and hence bondline temperature rise, scales roughly as (b*D^3*sin(gamma))^-0.5. A fit to eight evaluated points gives T-300 ~ 122*(X/1.218)^0.65, with X = (b*D^3*sin(gamma))^-0.5. Larger bluntness and diameter therefore lower both objectives at once, and a steeper angle lowers T at some cost in q and g. Peak g is set mainly by gamma and stays below 12 for |gamma| up to about 3.6-3.9 deg at large D. A high cone angle (about 70 deg) lets a very blunt nose (b about 1.1-1.3) stay geometrically valid, gives a low area-to-mass ratio, and keeps the shield mass fraction low. The plan is to push b up to about 1.1-1.3 at theta about 70, D up to about 3.0-3.2, and gamma to -3 to -3.8, while probing the g limit, the mass limit and the geometry boundary.
rounds.uncertainty: The geometry boundary is inferred from 20 samples. My fit of the nose-radius factor was inconsistent (about 1.8-1.95 times b*D/2), so designs with b >= 1.25 at theta=70 could still be invalid. The g model is extrapolated for large D and high theta. The T and q predictions come from a power-law fit to 8 points and may be off by 10-20%. The mass-fraction margin near D=3.2-3.3 depends on shield area, which I estimate only roughly.

rounds.observation: All 16 feasible designs sit in a narrow cluster: D 2.9-3.35 m, cone 55-70 deg, bluntness 0.5-1.15, gamma -3.0 to -3.9. C-11dcf14fd72e is the only feasible non-dominated point (287250 W/m2, 393.73 K). The hypervolume is about 0.885*0.375 = 0.332, so it is set entirely by that one point. With a 2.5e6 W/m2 reference against a 450 K one, 1 K of bondline temperature is worth roughly 40,000 W/m2 of peak flux. I should therefore push bondline temperature down first, then flux. Three limits bind: max_g (12 g), heatshield mass fraction (large D), and a geometry-validity boundary.
evidence: Mass fraction: 1 - margin divided by D^2 is nearly constant at 0.0877-0.0889 (C-11dcf14fd72e 0.0877, C-4f7f664531cd 0.0874, C-14caae5709dc 0.0889). It falls slightly with higher bluntness and cone angle. The mass limit is therefore D of about 3.37-3.38 m at b >= 1.15 and cone 70.

max_g: at gamma -3.5 it is 11.87 for D >= 3.25 (C-11dcf14fd72e, C-a687c9db7052, C-deeb5fd5f24a) and 11.77 for D 3.1 (C-cb5b9b5d5a6b). The slope is about 1.7 g/deg (C-dc1d6416cb31 to C-22c8ef75dedb to C-0be4678d643c). Gamma of about -3.57 is therefore the g limit at D 3.35.

Gamma trade: C-dc1d6416cb31 (gamma -3.0) vs C-e964c99bacf1 (gamma -3.4) at the same b, cone and D shows +11100 W/m2 and -4.56 K for 0.4 deg steeper. A steeper gamma is the cheapest way to lower bondline temperature.

Bluntness at D 3.1, cone 70: C-cb5b9b5d5a6b (b 1.1) 315290 W/m2, 397.73 K; C-4f7f664531cd (b 1.15) 312530 W/m2, 397.39 K. Lower b is worse: C-6e14665f4a23 (b 0.7) 402.47 K and C-6c22d4ab2deb (b 0.5) 408.52 K. Cone angle has little effect at fixed b (C-14caae5709dc vs C-7105f85b6659).

Geometry failures fit a rule with all 8 failed rows and the valid rows: cos(cone)*(2*b - 0.2) must be below 0.8. For example C-2e989122c857 gives 0.872, which predicts -22 mm against the reported -22.8 mm. C-de1dd6ca3952 gives -716 mm predicted and -715.7 mm reported. At cone 70, b must be at most about 1.24; at cone 68, at most about 1.14; at cone 69, at most about 1.19. I keep all proposals inside this rule with a margin.

C-63aaa0985529 (cone 29.7, b 0.52) and C-62348c286fc5 (cone 40, b 0.5) have bondline temperatures of 409.6 K and 418.35 K. Low bluntness and low cone are clearly worse, so the search should stay at high b and cone.
rounds.mechanism: Peak flux falls with larger nose radius (bluntness times D) and lower ballistic coefficient (larger D). Bondline temperature follows the integrated heat load, which is lower for steeper entry and for lower flux. Peak g is set mainly by gamma, with a weak dependence on D. The best design is therefore the largest D that the mass-fraction limit allows (about 3.36-3.38 m), the highest valid bluntness at cone 70 (about 1.2-1.24), and the steepest gamma with g under 12 (about -3.5 to -3.57). Shallower-gamma points at the same geometry add lower-flux, higher-temperature points for front coverage. The D^-1.4 flux scaling and the linear gamma slopes are empirical fits to this data. The soak-time argument is prior physical knowledge.
rounds.uncertainty: The g dependence on D and b is poorly resolved; D3.25, D3.3 and D3.35 give the same g at gamma -3.5, but D3.1 is lower. Points within 0.02 of g = 12 may fall either way. The mass-fraction coefficient at b > 1.15 is extrapolated, so the D 3.38 probe could go infeasible. The flux and temperature at gamma shallower than -2.6 are extrapolations; the temperature may rise nonlinearly. The b 1.24 and cone 70 geometry sits close to the validity boundary (predicted fore-cone length about 12 mm), so a failure is possible if my fitted rule is slightly off.

rounds.observation: Hypervolume is dominated by bondline temperature. The reference is 450 K, so a 1 K reduction is worth about 4x more area than a 10 kW/m2 heat-flux reduction. The feasible front sits at D=3.0-3.05 m, b=0.95-1.1, cone 68-70 deg, FPA -2.0 to -3.25 deg. From the margins, the limits are max_g = 12.0 and bondline = 450 K. Constraint behaviour: (1) Peak g is set almost only by FPA, about 9.63 at -2.0, 11.56 at -3.4, roughly 1.5 g/deg, so g reaches 12 near -3.7 deg. (2) Heatshield mass-fraction usage scales as D^2: margin is 0.21 at D=3.0, 0.41 at 2.6, 0.186 at 3.05, so it hits zero near D~3.37 at high cone angle. (3) Geometry failures match cos(cone) <= 0.4/(b-0.1), with Rn=b*D and shoulder radius 0.1*D. This reproduces the failing lengths for C-c28d2aecc04e and C-d03a6d571826. Larger D lowers both heat flux (roughly D^-1.4) and bondline temperature (about -20 K/m). Higher b and cone help slightly. The best unexplored region is D~3.2-3.37, b~1.17-1.25, cone 70, FPA -3.4 to -3.65. It pushes toward the g and mass limits, with a few shallower-FPA points to spread the front.
evidence: C-f5cd2c404e61 (D2.6,b1.1,c70,-3.3): T 411.3, HF 399.7k. C-2a1f2582e86f (D3.05, same b/c, -3.25): T 401.5, HF 315.8k. Larger D lowers both objectives at the same FPA.

C-a21c8a3f8776 (-2.0): g 9.63, T 420.6. C-764eef2a20fc (-3.4): g 11.56, T 401.6, g margin 0.036. Steeper FPA lowers T at about 10-14 K/deg and raises g at about 1.5 g/deg, so g=12 is reached near -3.7 deg.
C-0fb9b23734ce (D3.0,b1.17,c70,-3.15): HF 316.6k, T 403.2, mass margin 0.214. Compared with the b=1.0 rows, higher b is slightly better on both objectives and geometry is valid.

Mass margin vs D: 0.408 at 2.6 (C-f5cd2c404e61), 0.208 at 3.0 (C-a21c8a3f8776), 0.186 at 3.05 (C-2a1f2582e86f). This fits usage proportional to D^2 and gives zero margin near D~3.37. C-e0059024652c (D3.39) and C-029296252ff3 (D3.63) violate mass fraction.

Geometry failures C-d03a6d571826 (b1.34, cone 69.6) and C-c28d2aecc04e (b0.965, cone 46) match the rule cos(cone) <= 0.4/(b-0.1), with negative fore-cone length = deficit/tan(cone). So b<=1.25 at cone 70 is valid.
rounds.mechanism: Heating follows a Sutton-Graves law (from prior knowledge) that falls with nose radius (b*D) and with ballistic coefficient. A larger, blunter, high-drag capsule decelerates higher in the atmosphere and has a lower heat load, so bondline temperature falls. A steeper entry shortens the heating pulse and lowers bondline temperature, at the cost of higher peak g and heat flux. Mass fraction limits D, and g limits how steep the entry can be. The optimum for temperature should sit on both limits: D~3.3 m, cone 70 deg, b~1.2, FPA~-3.5 to -3.6. Shallow-FPA designs at the same D give lower heat flux and higher T, which fills the left side of the front.
rounds.uncertainty: The D and FPA trends are extrapolated beyond the explored range (D up to 3.37 vs 3.05 measured, FPA -3.65 vs -3.4). The mass-fraction margin near D 3.37 and the g margin near FPA -3.65 are thin, so several proposals may come out infeasible. The b=1.25 point sits close to the geometry boundary (rule derived from the failure messages). The bondline-temperature dependence on D is probably diminishing, so my T predictions may be a few K optimistic.

rounds.observation: All 20 round-2 proposals were wasted on the invalid corner (bluntness 1.25-1.35, cone 70, D around 3.36). The geometry check rejects any cone angle too small for the nose radius, and the fore cone length goes negative. At D=3.36 and cone 70, the overrun is -12.7 mm at b=1.30 and -33.7 mm at b=1.35, so the limit is near b=1.27. b=1.25 also failed a separate surrogate check (cd_fore outside its training hull). The only feasible designs sit at b=1.1-1.18, cone 68-70, D 3.2-3.3. Within that set, lower gamma gives lower heat flux and higher bondline temperature (about 264k W/m2 and 411 K at -2.2 deg, about 290k and 394 K at -3.5 deg). Peak g reaches about 11.83 at -3.5 deg and hits its 12 g limit near -3.6 deg. The mass-fraction margin shrinks as D grows (0.106 at D 3.2, 0.078 at 3.25, 0.046 at 3.3 with cone 68). This round stays inside the proven envelope and fills the front along gamma, D and mild bluntness changes.
evidence: C-b86d67fded52 (D 3.2, b 1.18, cone 70, gamma -2.2): 263.6k W/m2, 411.2 K, feasible. This is the low-flux end of the front.
C-51e48573fc56 (D 3.25, b 1.18, cone 70, gamma -3.5): 290.4k W/m2, 394.3 K, g margin 0.014. This is the low-temperature end.
C-114b79b08144 (gamma -3.7, b 1.1, D 3.2): g 12.136, infeasible. Together with C-84c7c9af373d (g 11.68 at -3.4) this puts the g limit near gamma -3.6 deg.
C-84c7c9af373d (D 3.3, cone 68): mass margin 0.0455, so D above about 3.35 risks the mass-fraction constraint.
C-2317645f3652, C-f986776067bd, C-733b361d9f0d and the b=1.35 rejections: bluntness at or above 1.25 with cone 69-70 is invalid or outside the hull, so keep b at or below about 1.22.
rounds.mechanism: Stagnation heating falls with nose radius, so higher bluntness and larger D help. Peak g is set mainly by gamma, and mass fraction limits D. Bondline temperature follows heat load, which is lower for a steeper, shorter pulse. Steep gamma near -3.55 to -3.6 lowers temperature while staying just under the g limit. Shallow gamma (-1.5 to -2.2) lowers peak flux and extends the front to the left. The hypervolume uses a 450 K reference, so a few kelvin of bondline temperature is worth much more than tens of thousands of W/m2. Effects of cone angle and of b between 1.18 and 1.22 are not well known from the data, so I probe them cautiously. These rely partly on prior physical knowledge, not only on the tables.
rounds.uncertainty: The g-versus-gamma slope is interpolated from designs with different D and b, so gamma of -3.58 to -3.6 may cross 12 g. The mass-fraction margin at D 3.34-3.36 is extrapolated. The b=1.20-1.22 points at cone 70 may fail the geometry or hull check. Effects of cone angle are essentially unobserved. Predicted fluxes and temperatures are linear interpolations and may be off by a few percent.

rounds.observation: Feasible front has only 2 points (C-a129e2c3933f, C-bbf9cdb0a525), both at the corner D~3.1-3.3, bluntness 1.2, cone 69.9. Reference spans (2.5e6 W/m2, 150 K of bondline temperature), so a 1 K drop in T is worth about 5x more hypervolume than the flux changes reachable here. Improvement must come from lowering bondline T while keeping max_g < 12 (limit inferred from margins) and mass margin >= 0. 14 of 40 evaluations returned no geometry. Failures cluster at bluntness >= 1.25 with cone <= 69.9, and at low cone angles for their bluntness.
evidence: max_g limit is 12: C-a129e2c3933f g=11.055, margin 0.0787. At D~3.0-3.3, g rises about 1.5-1.7 per deg of |gamma|: C-1e7b6fd1901c gamma -3.6 g=11.886 (margin 0.009), C-602600f85327 gamma -4.2 g=13.0 (infeasible). g depends only weakly on D (about +0.35 per m).

Bondline T falls with steeper gamma at fixed geometry, about 8-12 K/deg: C-602600f85327 (D3.2, gamma -4.2) 388.6 K vs C-a129e2c3933f (D3.3, gamma -3.0) 398.6 K. Shallow gamma is worse: C-eae9b8e0689a gamma -2.2 is 418 K.

Larger bluntness and cone lower T and flux at fixed D and gamma: C-8fd56d301a14 (b0.6, cone 45) 413.5 K/411k; C-b5d3475ab118 (b0.9, cone 62) 407.4 K; C-c12000ea6fcb (b1.0, cone 66.3) 406.4 K; C-5bc1f1f05670 (b1.1, cone 69.9, gamma -3.2) 403.1 K.

Mass-fraction margin depends on D and slightly on b/cone, not on gamma: D3.1 0.161 (C-bbf9cdb0a525), D3.2 0.106 (C-602600f85327), D3.3 0.0497 (C-a129e2c3933f), about -0.055 per 0.1 m. It hits zero near D~3.39. C-c97855c2d790 (D4.27) is -0.83.

Bluntness 1.25 (C-a554636d8035) fails the cd_fore convex-hull check. Bluntness 1.3 (C-ed967979f72a) gives an invalid geometry. Bluntness 1.2 at cone 69.9 is valid at D3.1-3.3 (C-a129e2c3933f, C-bbf9cdb0a525, C-602600f85327), and geometry validity looks independent of D since all lengths scale with D.
rounds.mechanism: This relies partly on prior Allen-Eggers-type scaling, calibrated to the data above. Stagnation flux scales about as sqrt(sin(gamma)/(Rn*CdA)), so larger D and bluntness lower flux, and shallower gamma lowers flux too. Bondline T follows the integrated heat load, which falls with larger nose radius, larger area (lower ballistic coefficient) and steeper gamma (shorter pulse). Steeper gamma costs peak deceleration g, capped at 12. D is capped by the heatshield mass fraction near 3.38. So the T-optimal region is max b/cone, D~3.3-3.38, and gamma near the g=12 boundary (about -3.55 to -3.6). Shallower-gamma variants at the same geometry extend the front toward lower flux with higher T.
rounds.uncertainty: The g boundary is tight: predicted g at gamma -3.55 to -3.6 is 11.9-12.0, so some of these will probably be infeasible. The mass-fraction edge near D3.37-3.38 is extrapolated linearly. The sqrt(sin gamma) flux scaling is approximate, and the C-602600f85327 point suggests flux may be about 3-5% lower than the scaling predicts. T-vs-gamma slope is about 8 K/deg near -3.5 but 12+ K/deg at shallow angles. Whether bluntness 1.22 at cone 70.0 passes the hull check is unknown. Effects of cone 70.0 vs 69.9 are unknown.

rounds.observation: The feasible front is essentially a one-dimensional gamma sweep at D≈3.36-3.37 m, bluntness 1.2, cone 70 deg. Flux rises about 24 kW/m2 per degree of steeper entry and bondline temperature falls about 10-14 K per degree. The front is closed on the steep side by max_g (limit about 12.0, reached near gamma -3.58) and on the large-D side by heatshield mass fraction (margin near 0 at D≈3.385). Cone 70 is the upper bound. Bluntness above about 1.2 at cone 70 returns 'no geometry' from surrogate extrapolation (4 failures at 1.22-1.24).
evidence: C-af5b99c2201c through C-df105fb625ce: at D 3.36-3.37, bluntness 1.2, cone 70, flux runs 243.6k to 277.1k and bondline 407.4 K to 391.7 K as gamma goes from -2.2 to -3.55. Both trends are smooth and near-linear.
C-2a109f1c4205 (gamma -3.58) has max_g margin -0.0005, and C-df105fb625ce (gamma -3.55) has margin +0.0037. The g limit therefore sits near gamma -3.57 at D 3.36.

C-ba7e63c2eae5 (D 3.2), C-757eacb03d61 (D 3.3) and C-77cd7361eded (D 3.1) all have higher flux and bondline temperature than D 3.36 at similar gamma. Larger D is better, and it is capped by mass fraction: margin 0.0149 at D 3.36 and 0.0090 at 3.37, extrapolating to zero near 3.385.

C-de59f8abeee6, C-ae614eb129f2, C-fc8f94cd132b and C-d5f231dc1870: bluntness 1.22-1.24 at cone 70 fails on the cd_fore hull. C-0a3bfd5f8237 (b 1.15, c 69) and C-19b8d4ea2ba7 (b 1.1, c 68) are slightly worse than b 1.2, c 70 at the same gamma.
C-ee99f55de428 and C-50a0a474d0f6 (small D, low bluntness) have flux of 0.75-1.5 MW/m2 and bondline above the 450 K limit. Only the large, blunt, high-cone corner is competitive.
rounds.mechanism: Peak flux falls with larger nose radius and lower ballistic coefficient (larger D, higher drag). Bondline temperature follows the integrated heat load, which falls for steeper entry and lower flux. Peak g rises with gamma steepness, and slightly with D at fixed gamma. The best trade-off is the largest D the mass limit allows, bluntness and cone at their buildable maxima, and gamma at the g limit. In hypervolume terms 1 K of bondline temperature is worth about 0.006, while 10 kW/m2 of flux is worth only about 0.004. So this round nudges D up to 3.38 (about -1.3 kW/m2 and -0.3 K versus 3.37), pushes gamma toward the g limit, and extends the shallow-gamma flux end. Small bluntness, cone and D probes are included to check whether the corner can move.
rounds.uncertainty: The g and mass-fraction limits are extrapolated linearly. The D 3.38 mass margin is estimated at about +0.003, and D 3.385 is nearly zero. Gamma -3.565 at D 3.38 is within about 0.001 in g of the limit. The hull boundary for bluntness above 1.2 is unknown and b 1.21 may fail. Predictions for shallow gamma below -2.2 extrapolate the flux and temperature slopes, and curvature could shift them by a few kelvin.

rounds.observation: Peak g is set almost entirely by flight-path angle and binds at a limit of 12 g. At D=3.3, b=1.17 and cone 70, g is 11.85 at -3.5 deg and 12.01 at -3.6 deg. Changing bluntness, cone angle or D by small amounts moves g by less than 0.05. Every point on the feasible front sits at the corner of the bounds: cone 70 (max), bluntness about 1.17, D about 3.3-3.37. That corner is capped by the heatshield mass fraction, whose margin falls about 0.58 per metre of D and does not depend on gamma. Larger D and slightly higher b lower both heat flux and bondline temperature. Bluntness 1.22 and 1.25 at cone 70 fail on aero surrogate extrapolation, while 1.20 works. The remaining headroom is D up to about 3.38 with b=1.2, cone 70, swept along the gamma trade-off from about -1.5 to -3.55 deg.
evidence: C-d3a7fa99fcee (D3.3) vs C-d706f33c18bc (D3.35), both b1.17 at -3.5 deg: heat flux 284.5k -> 278.4k, bondline 393.5 -> 392.6 K. Larger D helps both objectives.
C-70f28f0eabf2 (D3.1), C-cde6c1e46d6d (D3.2), C-c050b796618a (D3.3) at -3.6 deg: heat 314k / 300k / 287k, bondline 396.2 / 394.3 / 392.5 K. Larger D is better on both axes.
Mass margin vs D at b1.17: 0.0489 at 3.3, 0.0199 at 3.35, 0.0081 at 3.37 (C-a8aec30c684b). The extrapolated zero is about D=3.384. b1.2 gives a slightly higher margin (0.0497 at 3.3, C-cbb67c388863).
C-cbb67c388863 (b1.2, -3.55) beats the interpolated b1.17 series at the same gamma: 284.4k / 392.8 K vs about 285.8k / 393.0 K.
Same-D gamma sweep at D3.3/b1.17: C-5644bff69a09 (-1.6) 239k / 418 K to C-d3a7fa99fcee (-3.5) 284.5k / 393.5 K. g reaches 12.0 at about -3.59 deg (C-c050b796618a, margin -0.001).
C-425c523a5086, C-5b57439845df and C-e605b64e0636 (b1.22-1.25, cone 70) are rejected for extrapolation. The b limit at cone 70 lies between 1.20 and 1.22.
rounds.mechanism: This relies on the data plus prior Sutton-Graves reasoning. Peak heating falls as nose radius (b*D) grows, and the heat load falls as ballistic coefficient drops, so a larger D at high b and cone 70 helps both objectives. Steeper entry shortens the heating pulse and lowers bondline temperature, but raises peak heat flux and g, and g caps gamma near -3.57 deg. The geometry is therefore pushed to the mass-fraction edge (D about 3.38) and gamma is swept along the g limit. That shifts the whole front toward lower heat flux and lower temperature. A few probes test cone angle, b just above 1.2, and the mass edge.
rounds.uncertainty: The mass-fraction edge near D=3.384 is extrapolated linearly from three points. The D3.38 points near -3.55 deg have about 0.03 g of margin, and g may rise slightly with D. The cone-angle probes are not backed by data at high b, and mass or aero behaviour may differ. The b>1.2 probes may hit the surrogate hull and fail. Predicted heat-flux and temperature gains from D use an exponent fitted only on D 3.1-3.35.

rounds.observation: Both objectives are dominated by one corner of the design space. Every feasible front point has cone angle 70 (the upper bound), bluntness 1.15-1.2 and D 3.25-3.36 m. Temperature is what moves hypervolume: the flux reference is 2.5e6 W/m2, so flux differences of about 40k barely matter, while 1 K of bondline temperature is worth about 0.006 normalised HV. From the margins, the limits are max_g <= 12.0 and heatshield mass fraction, which behaves like margin ~ 0.0497 + 0.028*(b-1.2) - 0.5855*(D-3.3). This puts the D ceiling near 3.385 m and makes the mass margin almost independent of gamma and cone. Peak g is set mainly by gamma (about 1.8 g/deg near -3.55) with a small positive D dependence (about 0.53 g/m). Larger D lowers both flux and temperature (about -16 K/m in T, flux roughly D^-1.3), and steeper gamma lowers T at about 1 K per 0.1 deg. The best corner is therefore D about 3.375-3.383, b about 1.2, cone 70, gamma about -3.55 to -3.565. Geometry failures occur for b >= 1.3 and for lower cone angles at high b. Bluntness 1.22 fails the cd_fore hull at cone 70, so b must stay at or below about 1.2-1.21.
evidence: C-cbb67c388863 (D3.3,b1.2,g-3.55): T392.78, g11.933, mass margin 0.0497. C-6b7d0d55c053 (D3.34,b1.15): mass margin 0.02513. C-0e7e9141529e (D3.36,b1.15): 0.01342. These fit the linear-in-D mass-margin law, so D <= 3.384 at b1.2.

C-9dee12ef8e1a (D3.28,g-3.55) 11.923, C-a07aa6172ab6 (D3.3,g-3.53) 11.898, C-59753de6b401 (D3.25,g-3.58) 11.961, C-a7cedecd1f0d (D3.22,g-3.6) 11.981 give dg/dgamma about -1.8 per deg and dg/dD about +0.5 per m, so the g limit at D3.38 is about gamma -3.56.
C-a07aa6172ab6 (D3.3,b1.18) T393.11 vs C-9dee12ef8e1a (D3.28,b1.18) T393.27 vs C-cbb67c388863 (D3.3,b1.2) T392.78 show that larger D and b lower T and that b is a weak lever.

C-1b507004c89c and C-de929f2046c9 (b1.22, cone70) fail the cd_fore hull; C-9c1cc1a27672, C-ec5b30508673, C-ca010b12fec4 (b1.35) and C-f986776067bd (b1.3, cone 69) are invalid geometries. b is capped near 1.2 at cone 70.

Shallow-gamma points C-e735d4570166 (241k, 421 K), C-30939dece9a3 and C-d916d7265dfe (252k, 409 K) and the steep corner C-cbb67c388863 (284k, 392.8 K) leave gaps in the staircase between gamma -2.2 and -3.3, and none of them uses D above 3.36.
rounds.mechanism: Stagnation flux falls with nose radius and with lower ballistic coefficient (larger D), so D at its mass-fraction ceiling and the largest valid b minimise flux. Bondline temperature tracks heat load, which falls with a shorter and steeper pulse, so gamma should sit just inside the g limit. Because g rises only slightly with D while T falls with D, pushing D to about 3.38 and backing gamma off by about 0.02 deg gives a net T drop of about 1 K. Re-running the whole gamma sweep at D3.375 dominates the older D3.2-3.3 front points and fills the staircase gaps.
rounds.uncertainty: The mass margin at D 3.38-3.383 is only 0.001-0.003 and the linear fit could be off by that much, so those designs may violate heatshield_mass_fraction. The g margin at gamma -3.56/-3.568 is under 0.1%, and the local slope in gamma is only roughly known. b of 1.205-1.21 may hit the cd_fore hull failure. Flux and T predictions come from eyeballed local fits (D^-1.3 for flux, about -16 K/m and about 1 K per 0.1 deg for T). They are less certain at shallow gamma, where the T slope is steeper (about 1.3-1.6 K per 0.1 deg).

rounds.observation: All 9 feasible non-dominated designs sit on one ridge: bluntness 1.2, cone 69.9 deg, D 3.3-3.38 m, entry angle -2.2 to -3.58 deg. Hypervolume is dominated by the bondline temperature axis, because flux is only about 0.1 of the 2.5 MW/m2 reference range while T spans 392-408 K of a 150 K range. The binding limit is max_g <= 12, reached at about -3.58 deg, and the heatshield mass-fraction margin runs out near D of about 3.385 m. In the data, T falls with steeper angle (about -10 K/deg), falls with larger D (about -18 K/m) and falls slightly with higher bluntness. Flux rises with steeper angle (about +24 kW/m2 per deg) and falls with larger D (about -120 kW/m2 per m). The ridge is therefore best pushed to D = 3.38 (the largest D with a verified positive mass margin) across the whole angle range.
evidence: C-3dfb47a1c8a3: D 3.38 has mass margin 0.003 (D 3.35: 0.0207, D 3.37: 0.0089), so D 3.38 is the largest verified buildable diameter; the extrapolated zero crossing is near 3.385.

C-d8198ec304c5: D 3.33, -3.58 deg gives g = 11.994 (margin 0.0005) and T = 391.96 K. Fitting the 3.3 m rows (C-158e05f9d36e, C-5dab03f5d001, C-2cf973a097ba) gives dg/d|gamma| of about 1.65 per deg and dg/dD of about +0.38 per m.
C-f07c60fdbdae vs C-0c6e47855b5e vs C-944b08da02c1: lowering bluntness from 1.2 to 1.1 raises T by about 0.65 K and flux by about 5 kW/m2 and lowers the mass margin, so b = 1.2 is best.
C-bcce2808c9b8 and C-a554636d8035 (b 1.22-1.25) fail the cd_fore convex hull, and C-ed967979f72a (b 1.3, cone 69.9) fails geometry, so b > 1.2 is not reachable.
C-404e4e066a3e and C-b76a72930094: the shallow end (-2.2, -2.4 deg) gives 246-250 kW/m2 at 405-408 K. Extending to -1.5 deg has not been tried.
C-02335773e828, C-2d91d8d713d7 and C-c97855c2d790: steeper angles (-6 to -7.4 deg) reach lower T but have g of 16-19, so they are infeasible and not competitive.
rounds.mechanism: This relies partly on prior Allen-Eggers-type reasoning, calibrated to local linear fits of the data. A larger D at fixed mass lowers the ballistic coefficient, so the vehicle decelerates higher in the atmosphere and its heat pulse is smaller. A larger nose radius (bluntness and D) lowers stagnation flux. A steeper angle shortens the heat pulse and lowers integrated load and bondline T, but raises peak g and flux. Peak g is set mainly by entry angle, with a weak D dependence, so the g <= 12 wall caps the steepness. Mass fraction depends on D, bluntness and cone angle but not on entry angle. The best achievable points therefore have D just under the mass limit, b = 1.2, cone near 70 deg, and entry angle chosen along the trade-off curve. I propose to shift the whole known front to D = 3.38 (about 0.5 K lower T and 3-4 kW/m2 lower flux at each angle), extend it shallow to -1.5 deg, and spend four slots probing bluntness and cone sensitivity.
rounds.uncertainty: The linear fits for g, T and flux were calibrated on D 3.2-3.38 and s = 2.2-3.6. Predictions at -1.5 to -2.1 deg extrapolate beyond the measured shallow end, and T there may be off by a few K. The g margin at -3.55 deg is only about 0.2%, and I am relying on the fitted slope. The four exploratory points (lower cone or bluntness) may fail geometry or the hull check, since the buildable cone/bluntness boundary is only known coarsely. I have not used the higher-fidelity simulator, so high-fidelity effects such as real-gas heating and ablation are not represented.

rounds.observation: Every non-dominated point comes from one family: D≈3.38 m, bluntness 1.2, cone 70 deg, with only flight-path angle varied. Along it flux rises from 228k to 275k W/m2 and bondline temperature falls from 418 K to 391 K as entry steepens. max_g (about 12 at gamma≈-3.57) and the mass-fraction limit (D<~3.3855 m) are the binding constraints. Bluntness and cone are pinned at the edge of the aero surrogate's hull. Bluntness 1.21 or more fails at cone 70, and cone 69 fails at bluntness 1.2. Smaller-D, lower-bluntness, lower-cone designs are clearly dominated. The remaining gains are small: a slightly larger D and a denser gamma sweep.
evidence: C-733cdcb996ae (D 3.385, gamma -3.5) gives 272900 W/m2 / 391.77 K, against 273480 / 391.85 for C-41b2ddb7397c (D 3.38, same gamma). Larger D dominates slightly, and its mass margin is only 0.000145.
Mass margin is independent of gamma (0.003097 across the D 3.38 sweep) and falls about 0.59 per metre of D. That puts the limit near D≈3.3855, so I keep D=3.385.

max_g at D 3.38 is 11.881 at -3.5, 11.963 at -3.55 and 11.989 at -3.565. C-2a109f1c4205 (D 3.36, -3.58) gives 12.006 and is infeasible, so the g limit sits near gamma≈-3.57. D changes g only weakly (about +0.4 per m).
C-3d41ce848a30, C-98457c6f78bd, C-ae614eb129f2 and others show that bluntness above 1.2 or cone below 70 at bluntness 1.2 hits surrogate extrapolation and returns no metrics.
Off-family designs such as C-22c8ef75dedb (322k, 395.7 K, infeasible), C-960c10206981 and C-ee99f55de428 are worse in flux or temperature than the D 3.38 family.
rounds.mechanism: Peak flux falls with larger nose radius and lower ballistic coefficient, so the largest D that meets the mass limit is best. Peak g is set almost entirely by gamma, so it caps steepness at about -3.57. Bondline temperature falls with steeper entry, so the best designs sit at the g limit. I have no data suggesting another geometry beats this family, so I refine it: D=3.385 for a small uniform gain, and a denser gamma sweep including points just inside the g limit. Interpolated values come from the D 3.38 sweep with a D correction of about -0.2% flux and -0.08 K.
rounds.uncertainty: The main risk is the g margin near gamma -3.56 to -3.568, where I estimate g at 11.99-11.996 against a limit of 12. Whether bluntness 1.205 lies inside the surrogate hull is unknown, and that probe may return no geometry. Gains per point are tiny (about 0.2% flux, 0.1 K). The reduced-order model's own noise or discreteness could exceed them. No other region has been shown to be promising.

rounds.observation: The feasible front is one geometry (D≈3.38, b=1.2, cone=70) swept in flight-path angle. Heat flux runs from 227.7k W/m2 at gamma=-1.5 to 274.7k at -3.55, and bondline temperature falls from 418 K to 391.4 K. Three constraints pin this corner. The g limit (about 12) caps gamma near -3.57. The heatshield mass fraction caps D near 3.385. The surrogate hull blocks b>1.2 at cone 70, and cone<70 at b=1.2 gives invalid geometry. Steeper gamma is infeasible (g margins go negative from -3.6), and smaller D or other geometries are dominated. The remaining gains are small refinements of the corner and denser coverage of the front.
evidence: C-d67ebd910866 to C-27aed1c1ecfd: the front is monotone in gamma (HF 227.7k to 274.7k W/m2, T 418.0 K to 391.4 K) at D=3.38, b=1.2, cone=70.
C-27aed1c1ecfd has g margin 0.003 at gamma=-3.55, and C-c050b796618a is infeasible on max_g at -3.6, so gamma must be no steeper than about -3.57.
C-a201e4576c17 (D=3.384) has mass margin 0.00074, against 0.0031 for D=3.38 and 0.0149 for D=3.36. Extrapolating, the mass limit is at D≈3.385.

rounds.observation: The feasible front is a one-dimensional curve traced by flight-path angle at D~3.375-3.38 m, bluntness 1.2, cone 70 deg (the variable upper bounds). Larger D lowers both flux (about -119k W/m2 per m) and T (about -18 K/m). Lower b is worse on both objectives. Bluntness 1.205 and above at cone 70 fails the cd_fore convex-hull check, and b>=1.3 gives invalid geometry. rounds.mechanism: Stagnation heating falls with nose radius (b*D/2) and with lower ballistic coefficient (larger D), so D and b are best at their caps. Bondline temperature follows heat load, which drops for steeper, shorter pulses. Peak g is set mainly by gamma, so the front is traced by gamma up to the g=12 limit. The D cap comes from mass fraction, which scales with D^2. Moving D from 3.375 to 3.384 lowers flux by about 1.1k W/m2 and T by about 0.16 K at every gamma. This shifts the whole front down slightly. Bondline T falls as the pulse shortens at steeper gamma. Peak g rises with gamma, which caps gamma near -3.57. The front is therefore a one-parameter curve in gamma. Bondline temperature falls with steeper gamma because the soak is shorter. Peak g depends almost only on gamma, with a weak positive dependence on D. The front is therefore a one-parameter curve in gamma. It ends at the g limit on the steep side and at the -1.5 deg bound on the shallow side. Bluntness, cone and D sit at their buildable maxima. About half of this batch densifies the curve, two proposals push to the g limit and D limit, and the rest probe interior bluntness and D values to check that nothing off the curve is better.

rounds.observation: The front is a one-dimensional gamma sweep at a single geometry corner: D=3.384, b=1.2, cone=70. Peak heat flux runs 227k to 275k W/m2 and bondline temperature 418 K to 391 K. I therefore spend this round on filling gamma gaps at a marginally larger D, and I rely on data-fitted local sensitivities rather than new physics.

Bondline temperature follows heat load, which falls with steeper entry and larger D. Larger D is limited by the mass fraction, larger b by the surrogate hull, and steeper gamma by max_g. The design is boxed in at D=3.3848, b=1.2, cone=70, so the only free direction is gamma. The D increase from 3.384 to 3.3845 or 3.3848 is a tiny but dominating improvement, kept inside the estimated mass-fraction limit.

rounds.observation: The front is a one-dimensional gamma sweep at the corner D~3.384, bluntness 1.2, cone 70. Every other variable is pinned by a limit: D by heatshield mass fraction (margin ~0 at D~3.385), cone at its 70 deg bound, bluntness by the aero-surrogate hull and geometry limit near b=1.2, and gamma by max_g=12 near -3.57. Round 2 (20 geometry failures) shows the danger of leaving this corner, so I stay on it and fill gaps and push the edges.

C-099cae65259a (b 1.1), C-8efdd90862a0 (b 1.15, cone 69) and C-26610a6c01d5 (b 1.0, cone 68) violate mass fraction and have higher flux and T than b 1.2, cone 70, so lower b or cone is worse.
C-de929f2046c9, C-207a027e9dd5, C-4d9cd4c2b38d (b 1.205-1.22) fail hull extrapolation, and C-f986776067bd, C-9c1cc1a27672 (b 1.3-1.35) fail geometry, so b cannot exceed ~1.2.
C-114b79b08144 (D 3.2, b 1.1, gamma -3.7) has T 393.8 K and is g-infeasible, so smaller D costs T and buys little g.
rounds.mechanism: Flux falls with nose radius (b*D/2) and with lower ballistic coefficient (larger D). T falls with a shorter, steeper entry pulse and with larger D. g is set almost entirely by gamma, at roughly 1.66 g/deg, with only a weak dependence on D. The feasible optimum therefore lies at the D, b and cone bounds, and the front is traced by gamma from -1.5 to -3.57. Extra hypervolume can only come from filling gaps between existing gamma points and from tiny D increases up to the mass cap (about 0.02% in flux). This rests partly on prior knowledge of the ~1/sqrt(Rn) heating scaling, which I did not check against the data.

The D=3.3851-3.3852 points sit within 1e-4 of the mass-fraction limit and the gamma=-3.568 points within 4e-4 of the g limit, so they may flip to infeasible if the margin is slightly nonlinear. rounds.observation: The feasible front is a one-parameter curve in flight_path_angle at the corner D≈3.38, bluntness 1.2, cone 70. Along it, peak flux runs 227.7k to 275.2k W/m2 and bondline T runs 418.0 K to 391.1 K. Three limits pin that corner. Peak g <= 12 caps gamma near -3.572. Heatshield mass fraction caps D near 3.385. The cd_fore surrogate hull caps bluntness at about 1.2 for cone about 70. Every other explored region is either dominated or infeasible on max_g or mass fraction. rounds.mechanism: This relies partly on prior Allen-Eggers-type reasoning, calibrated to the data. Peak g in a ballistic-type entry is set mainly by gamma and hardly by geometry, so gamma is capped near -3.57. Flux falls with nose radius and area (about D^-1.4 here, from the C-fe69bc352dbe/C-32c1a76f8425 pair), and bondline T falls with heat load, which is lower for larger D and steeper gamma. The mass-fraction constraint stops D growing past about 3.385, and the hull stops b growing past about 1.2. The best design therefore stays at the corner and moves along gamma. Raising D to 3.384-3.385 gives about -0.17 to -0.2% flux and -0.07 K everywhere, a small gain. The remaining slots sample gamma gaps and probe hull edges.

The mass margin at D=3.384-3.385 is only about 0.0001-0.0008, and the g margin at gamma about -3.57 is about 1e-4, so feasibility is marginal. I extrapolate the D dependence of g and mass margin linearly from two or three close points. The hull probes at b=1.205 and cone 69.6 could return a no-geometry failure. rounds.observation: The front is a one-parameter family at D=3.385, bluntness 1.2, cone 70, swept in flight path angle. rounds.mechanism: Peak flux falls with nose radius (bluntness x D) and with ballistic coefficient (larger D), so D, bluntness and cone are pushed to their limits. Peak g depends mainly on gamma, with a weak positive dependence on D of about 0.4 g/m. Bondline temperature falls as entry gets steeper because the soak time is shorter. The trade-off is therefore set by gamma alone, from shallow (low flux, hot bondline) to the g cap (higher flux, cooler bondline). Physics here is from the data plus prior knowledge: in Allen-Eggers theory peak g is independent of ballistic coefficient. I expect more gamma points to add only a small hypervolume gain, and the D and gamma micro-tweaks to add almost none.

The micro-tweaks near the mass and g limits could fall just over either limit, since I am extrapolating locally linear slopes to about 1e-5 relative margin. The interpolated flux and temperature values are linear estimates. The true curve is convex, so actual values should sit slightly below them. I have no data on any geometry outside this family that could beat it.

rounds.mechanism: This relies on the data plus prior Sutton-Graves reasoning. Flux falls with nose radius (bD) and with ballistic coefficient, and bondline temperature falls with heat load, so the best designs have the largest D that the mass fraction allows. A larger b and cone 70 give the flattest forebody with the least area per D^2. Steeper entry lowers bondline temperature at the cost of flux and g, so the corner is set by mass fraction, max_g and the hull. The remaining gains are small: (1) probing b just above 1.2, where a 0.4 to 1 percent larger nose radius trims flux by ~0.2 to 0.5 percent; (2) pushing gamma to the g limit; (3) filling gaps along the curve, since every interpolated gamma is non-dominated; (4) two cheap probes of whether lower b or smaller D lowers g enough to allow steeper gamma.

Predicted g near the limit is uncertain by about 0.01 g. Interpolated flux and temperature values are linear and should be accurate to about 0.3 percent. The cone-69.8 offset (about +0.05% flux, -0.12 K) gives non-dominated points spaced along the gamma range. Gamma gap-fillers at cone 70 raise coverage of the convex front. Cone probes at 69.2-69.7 test where the hull edge lies.
rounds.uncertainty: The hull edge in cone at b=1.2 is unknown, since cone 69.0 failed and 69.8 passed, so the cone 69.2-69.7 probes may fail. The cone offset effect at other gammas is inferred from one point. Predictions for gap-fillers are linear interpolation. Feasibility at gamma -3.5703 is marginal.

rounds.observation: The front is a one-parameter curve in flight_path_angle_deg. Every good design sits at D=3.3852, bluntness=1.2, cone=70. Bluntness and cone are capped by the aero-surface convex hull, since the 1.205 to 1.24 bluntness and cone=69 probes all failed extrapolation. Peak g is capped at 12 by gamma near -3.5703. Normalised hypervolume has plateaued at 0.3556 over the last five rounds. With one round and 24 evaluations left, the remaining gain is filling the gaps along the gamma line.
evidence: C-9af34480dd37 and C-42bf20532268: gamma=-3.5703 gives g=12.0 with margin ~1.4e-5 to 2e-5, so this is the steep end of the front.
C-895ab2d00f94: gamma=-1.5 is the shallow bound, with flux 227200 and T=417.87.
Consecutive front points at gamma -1.5, -1.8, -1.9, -2.15, -2.3, -2.4 and -2.72 leave gaps of 0.1 to 0.32 deg. Flux and temperature vary smoothly and nearly linearly between them.
C-2a109f1c4205 (D=3.36) has flux 277780 against 274560 at D=3.3852. Smaller D therefore costs flux and gives no compensating g benefit, so the D=3.3852 line stays dominant.
C-7112b6b29bcf, C-14444dd6b10a, C-9961e7e6987c and C-67c6047be079: lowering bluntness or cone raises flux and violates the mass fraction, so they are dominated.
Rows C-de59f8abeee6, C-ae614eb129f2, C-3d41ce848a30, C-98457c6f78bd and C-ea0e387c4c00 (geometry failures): stepping outside the hull wastes evaluations.
rounds.mechanism: Flux falls with nose radius and lower ballistic coefficient, and bondline temperature falls with steeper entry because the soak is shorter. This is partly prior knowledge and partly fitted to the front rows. Since D, bluntness and cone are all at their limits, only gamma trades the two objectives. Filling gaps in gamma with linearly interpolated flux and temperature adds small but certain non-dominated points, and every proposal stays at the known-feasible D=3.3852.
rounds.uncertainty: The interpolated values assume smooth, near-linear variation. The true curve is slightly convex, so actual values may sit a little below the linear estimates, which would only help. Some gamma values may already have been evaluated in rows I cannot see. Gains per point are tiny because the front is nearly saturated. No exploratory off-line designs are included, since the data give no evidence that any beats this family.

rounds.observation: The front is a single one-parameter curve. Every non-dominated point sits at D~3.385, b=1.2, cone=70 and differs only in flight-path angle. Flux runs from 227k W/m2 at gamma=-1.5 to 274.5k at -3.5702, while bondline T falls from 417.9 K to 391.1 K. Each of the other three variables is pinned by a wall: D by the mass fraction (margin ~3e-5), b and cone by the surrogate hull (b=1.202 and cone 69 both fail), and gamma by max_g=12 (about 1.7 g/deg). Other geometries such as C-ea6fa32467e5 (b 0.9, cone 66) are dominated. Only 21 evaluations remain, so I fill the gaps in the gamma sweep at fixed geometry. This should trim the staircase area under the front with almost no risk of geometry failure.
evidence: C-b8e5f12114a1 (gamma -1.5) and C-a21e478c2d2d (gamma -3.5702, max_g margin 1.2e-5) are the two ends of the feasible front; all 12 listed non-dominated points share D=3.385, b=1.2, cone=70.

Flux and T are smooth and nearly linear in gamma between neighbours, e.g. C-255298c956e9 (-2.58: 250860, 402.02) and C-74cfdfd96a8c (-2.78: 255600, 399.55). Linear interpolation should therefore be accurate.
Hull and geometry failures at b=1.202-1.208 (C-507815483127 etc.), cone 69 (C-d0f9b054a40c) and cone 62-64 (C-17a9b770e63c) show that b, cone and D cannot be pushed further.
C-ea6fa32467e5 (b 0.9, cone 66, gamma -3.5) gives 294k W/m2 and 394.6 K, dominated by C-8d69d1842e32 (272.9k, 391.76 K). Lower b or cone gives no gain.
Peak g of 11.88 at -3.5 and 12.0 at -3.5702 (C-a21e478c2d2d) confirm gamma is capped near -3.5702.
rounds.mechanism: This relies on the data plus prior Sutton-Graves reasoning. Peak flux falls with nose radius b*D and with ballistic coefficient, so the largest D that meets the mass fraction, with maximal b and cone, is best. Steeper entry shortens the heating pulse, which lowers bondline T at the cost of higher peak flux and g. Peak g is nearly independent of D and depends on gamma. The trade-off is therefore traced only by gamma at the box corner, and the remaining gain is from denser sampling of that curve, especially the g-limited end.
rounds.uncertainty: The predictions are interpolations between measured neighbours. The main risks are the max_g margin at gamma about -3.565 to -3.5703, which is under 1e-4 g from the limit, and the mass margin, which is untouched because D is not changed. The hypervolume gain from these points is expected to be very small (~1e-4 or less).

rounds.observation: The feasible front is effectively a one-parameter curve in flight_path_angle at D=3.385, bluntness=1.2, cone=70. Flux rises from 227k W/m2 at -1.5 deg to 274.6k at -3.5703 deg, and bondline T falls from 417.9 K to 391.1 K. Diameter is capped by heatshield_mass_fraction (margin about 1.4e-4). Gamma is capped by max_g at about -3.5703 deg. Bluntness above 1.2, or cone or D below the corner, hits the cd_fore convex-hull refusal or a geometry failure. Hypervolume gains have fallen to about 1e-5 per round, so the last 25 evaluations fill gaps in the curve and probe the tiny remaining D and b headroom.
evidence: C-948029610632 to C-8efe13d24286: at D=3.385, b=1.2, cone=70, gamma from -1.5 to -3.5703 gives flux 227k to 275k W/m2 and T 417.9 to 391.1 K, with max_g reaching 12.0 at -3.5703.
C-8efe13d24286 has max_g margin 3.2e-5, and C-112b974177e0 (D=3.38, gamma -3.572) violates max_g. Gamma is therefore pinned near -3.570.
C-948029610632 has mass margin 1.449e-4 and C-013d6de46fd0 (D=3.384) has 7.356e-4. That slope puts the mass limit near D=3.38525, so D=3.3851 to 3.3852 should stay feasible.

C-a554636d8035, C-bcce2808c9b8, C-2375647d7e43, C-3d41ce848a30, C-dcc9bfd9f503 and C-166a3a760ccb all fail on cd_fore extrapolation. b>1.2 or cone<70 combined with D away from 3.385 is unsafe, so I keep the corner values.
Gamma gaps on the curve with no evaluated point at D=3.385 and cone=70: -1.5 to -1.7, -1.95 to -2.35, -2.35 to -2.7, -2.7 to -3.05 and -3.1 to -3.4 (C-13574164271b, C-2f9f349729bd, C-af77f965ad8e).
rounds.mechanism: This relies partly on prior Allen-Eggers-type reasoning and partly on the data. At the mass-limited corner (D, b, cone), flux and bondline T depend mainly on gamma. Steeper entry raises peak flux through sqrt(sin gamma) and shortens the heat pulse, which lowers the integrated load and bondline T. The g limit caps steepness. Local linear interpolation of the neighbouring evaluated points gives the predicted flux and T. Since D, b and cone are pinned by constraints, the only remaining upside is interpolation in gamma and a tiny D increase (about +0.0002 m).
rounds.uncertainty: The main uncertainty is whether D=3.3851 to 3.3852 or b=1.201 triggers the cd_fore hull refusal or violates the mass fraction. The gain from either is negligible. Predictions from interpolation should be accurate to about 0.1 percent in flux and 0.1 K in T. Max_g near -3.57 deg is marginal.

rounds.observation: Only one evaluation remains. All 85 front members appear to lie on a one-parameter family: D=3.3852 (mass-fraction limit), bluntness 1.2 and cone 70 (edge of the aero surrogate hull) held fixed, with flight-path angle setting the trade-off. Flux rises and bondline temperature falls as gamma steepens. Gamma is capped at about -3.5703 by max_g and at -1.5 by the variable bound. Changing D, bluntness or cone has failed repeatedly, through a mass-fraction violation, a geometry failure or surrogate extrapolation, so I leave them alone. The widest visible gap in the listed gamma coverage is between -1.5 and -1.73, so I fill it.
evidence: C-895ab2d00f94 (gamma -1.5): flux 227200, Tb 417.87, feasible, max_g margin 0.2317.
C-9fa328647bb7 (gamma -1.73): flux 231790, Tb 414.12, feasible.
C-adca91e5651d (gamma -1.77) and C-e187d3d3634a (gamma -1.85) show the local slope: about 20000 W/m2 per deg in flux and about -16 K per deg in temperature.

Every off-family neighbour was either infeasible or failed: bluntness at or below 1.15 gives a mass-fraction violation (C-7112b6b29bcf), and bluntness above 1.2 or cone below 70 with D near 3.38 gives surrogate extrapolation failures (C-ae614eb129f2, C-98457c6f78bd).
rounds.mechanism: Bluntness, cone and D are pinned at their limits, so only gamma trades the two objectives. Shallower entry gives lower peak flux and a longer soak, hence a hotter bondline. Peak g is about 9.2 to 9.4 here, well inside the 12 g limit. A point at gamma -1.62 lies between two known front points. Flux and temperature vary smoothly and slightly convexly with gamma, so it should sit just below the linear chord in both objectives. That makes it weakly non-dominated and a small certain hypervolume gain.
rounds.uncertainty: Rows not shown may already cover gamma near -1.62, in which case the gain is negligible. The list of non-dominated points is truncated (12 shown of 85). The interpolated values could be off by a few hundred W/m2 or about 0.3 K. Feasibility is very likely, because all margins are comfortable except the mass fraction, which does not depend on gamma.

rounds.observation: Only 1 of 20 evaluated designs is feasible (C-ee454ee3df8f: 578.9 kW/m2, 432.1 K). 11 of 20 failed geometry. Constraint limits back-calculated from the margins: max_g 12, bondline temperature 450 K. Heatshield mass fraction grows steeply with diameter and is binding by about D 3.3 m. The geometry failures fit a single rule. Taking nose radius as roughly bluntness*D, the fore cone goes negative when bluntness*cos(cone_half_angle) is above about 0.5. Every valid row has B*cos(theta) <= 0.46 and every failed row has >= 0.53. Peak flux scales roughly as D^-1.65 * B^-0.5 * sqrt(sin|gamma|). Bondline temperature falls with lower flux and with steeper entry. max_g rises with steeper entry, about 10.8 g at -3.1 deg and 13.2 g at -4.1 deg, so gamma is capped near -3.6 deg.
evidence: Flux scaling: 63010 (B 0.315, D 2.08) has 900 kW/m2 against 579 kW/m2 for ee454 (B 0.674, D 2.23) at nearly the same gamma, which fits flux ~ 1/sqrt(nose radius). Larger D gives much lower flux: f84c (D 3.34) 349 kW/m2 at -5.5 deg, 4cf8 (D 4.05) 302 kW/m2 at -4.1 deg.
g limit: ee454 10.8 g at -3.12 deg, 63010 10.96 g at -3.18 deg, 4cf8 13.16 g at -4.07 deg, fae3 9.24 g at -1.75 deg. About 2.5 g per degree puts the 12 g limit near -3.6 deg.
Bondline temperature: fae3 at -1.75 deg is 470.7 K (infeasible) while 4cf8 at -4.07 deg is 387 K. Shallow entry means a long heat pulse and a hot bondline.
Current hypervolume is 0.092. That equals the feasible point's (1-579/2500)*(1-132/150). The bondline-temperature axis has a lot of headroom to gain.
rounds.mechanism: Stagnation heating falls with nose radius (~Rn^-0.5). Nose radius here is roughly B*D, and larger D also lowers the ballistic coefficient, so flux drops strongly with D. Bondline temperature follows the heat load: lower flux and steeper, shorter entries both cool it. The g limit caps steepness at about -3.6 deg and the mass-fraction limit caps D near 3.2 m. The best region is therefore large D (2.8-3.3 m), large bluntness paired with a large cone angle so that B*cos(theta) stays about 0.42-0.44 (geometry-valid), and gamma about -3.3 to -3.6 deg. The flux, temperature and g scalings come from fitting the 9 valid rows plus general hypersonic-heating knowledge (stagnation-point heating ~ Rn^-0.5).
rounds.uncertainty: The geometry rule is fitted from 20 rows. The exact nose-radius definition is not verified, because the reported negative lengths only partly match my formula. The flux exponent on D and the temperature model are extrapolations from few points. Whether max_g depends on D or cone angle is unknown, so the g boundary near -3.6 to -3.8 deg is uncertain. The mass-fraction dependence on cone angle and bluntness is only roughly inferred.

rounds.observation: The front is a one-parameter curve in flight_path_angle_deg at the corner D≈3.385 m, bluntness 1.2, cone 70°. Peak g caps gamma near -3.5703, and the heatshield mass fraction caps D at about 3.3852 m (margin 2.7e-5). The bluntness and cone perturbations near the corner all failed: 'cd_fore' surrogate extrapolation, or overlapping nose sphere and shoulder torus. With 11 evaluations left, the only safe hypervolume gain is to fill gaps along the gamma curve at the D=3.3852 corner, since the rest of the front is already dense.
evidence: C-6daecae7b30e (-1.5°): flux 227200 W/m2, T 417.87 K. C-c2d1addc0c7e (-1.75°): 232230 W/m2, 413.81 K. The gap between them is the largest on the front and has no evaluated points at D=3.3852.

C-8efe13d24286 (-3.5703°, D=3.385) has max_g 12.0000, margin 3.2e-5. C-96e48a93fd32 (-3.5695°, D=3.3852) has margin 1.2e-4. C-112b974177e0 (-3.572°) is infeasible on max_g, so gamma is capped near -3.5703.

C-4e45b26ae0a9, C-166a3a760ccb, C-3d41ce848a30, C-dcc9bfd9f503, C-bcce2808c9b8 and C-2375647d7e43 all failed on cd_fore extrapolation. C-ed967979f72a failed on geometry. No bluntness or cone change should be attempted.

D=3.3852 shows a mass-fraction margin of 2.677e-5 against 1.449e-4 at D=3.385, and flux and T are marginally better at the larger D. Every proposal therefore keeps D=3.3852, inherited from the parent.
rounds.mechanism: This relies on the data and on prior Allen-Eggers-type reasoning. Peak flux scales roughly as sqrt(sin(gamma)) and rises with steeper entry. The heat pulse shortens with steeper entry, so bondline T falls. Peak g rises with gamma and sets the steep limit. Locally, flux and T are smooth and nearly linear in gamma. The proposals interpolate between evaluated neighbours at D=3.3852 (slopes about +20 to +24 kW/m2 per degree in flux and -12 to -16 K per degree in T). This adds coverage of the trade-off curve without any surrogate-hull or geometry risk.

The main risk is the two points nearest the g limit (-3.565°, -3.57°), where max_g margin is around 1e-4. This is a reduced-order model and I have not seen behaviour beyond the evaluated range. Expected hypervolume gain is very small (about 1e-5).

rounds.observation: Only 1 of 16 feasible designs is non-dominated (C-ea2223901bd4: 295k W/m2, 396.2 K). Temperature falls with larger D, higher bluntness and cone angle, and steeper entry. Feasibility is capped by max_g (about 12, reached near gamma -3.6) and by heatshield mass fraction (margin near zero at D of about 3.35). Bluntness of 1.25 with cone of 70 deg, and B=1.2 with cone 69 at D=3.0, returned extrapolation failures. Low cone angles at high bluntness return invalid geometry.
evidence: C-94a9f7a46f9b (D3.2, B1.2, c69.5, -3.8) reaches 392.2 K but max_g is 12.309, so it is infeasible. C-1618bda1fac0 at -3.7 gives 12.139. This implies about 1.7 g per degree and a gamma limit near -3.6 at D of about 3.2.
g at fixed gamma rises about 0.45 per metre of D. C-ea2223901bd4 (D3.3, -3.4) gives 11.686 and C-963d4cdbada1 (D3.2, -3.5) gives 11.816. This supports about -3.55 as the limit at D of about 3.3.

Temperature falls about 2.2 K per 0.1 m of D. C-c0f89c462bd0 (D3.1) is 400.8 K and C-963d4cdbada1 (D3.2) is 398.0 K at the same gamma. C-7ef0b45caabb (D3.1) is 398.4 K and C-2b74a3ea4aeb (D3.0) is 399.2 K.

Mass-fraction margin shrinks about 0.06 per 0.1 m of D. It is 0.209 at D3.0 (C-2b74a3ea4aeb), 0.097 at D3.2 (C-1618bda1fac0) and 0.035 at D3.3 (C-ea2223901bd4). C-f84c59a3cc23 at D3.34 has 0.010. D of about 3.36 is therefore near the limit.
B/cone effect: C-94a9f7a46f9b (B1.2, c69.5) is about 1.4 K cooler and about 7k lower in flux than C-1618bda1fac0 (B1.0, c66), after correcting for gamma.
Shallower gamma lowers flux slightly but raises temperature about 1 K per 0.1 deg. C-d2c4b79f3796 (-3.3) is 402.9 K and C-2b74a3ea4aeb (-3.6) is 399.2 K, at similar D.

Extrapolation failures: C-40f2342796ee (3.0,1.2,69), C-0202524b57fd (2.6,1.25,70) and C-1d24bfa5f84e (2.8,1.25,70). C-94a9f7a46f9b (3.2,1.2,69.5) evaluated fine, so B of 1.2 at cone 69.5 is the edge of the known-safe region.
rounds.mechanism: Heat flux and bondline temperature both fall as ballistic coefficient falls and effective nose radius rises. Larger D, higher B and larger cone angle all do this, since drag coefficient and nose radius grow. Steeper entry shortens the heat pulse and lowers temperature, but raises peak g. The optimum is therefore pinned at three corners at once: D near the mass-fraction limit (about 3.35), gamma near the g limit (about -3.5 to -3.6), and B/cone near the edge of the aero-surrogate hull (B1.1-1.2, cone 67-69.5). This is largely inferred from the 40 rows, with standard entry-heating physics only as background. The simple additive sensitivities I use are local linear fits and may be off near the constraint edges.
rounds.uncertainty: The margins on max_g (about 0.003 to 0.02) and mass fraction (about 0 to 0.05) are within my model error, so several proposals near the edge may come back infeasible. Hull behaviour for B of 1.2 or more is unclear because it may depend on D. The effect of gamma on the mass fraction is not separated from the effect of D. The shallow-gamma flux gain is extrapolated from few points.

rounds.observation: The feasible front is 3 points clustered at D~3.34, B=1.2, cone=69.5, gamma -2.8 to -3.5, with normalised HV 0.347. Fitting the near-front rows gives limits set by three constraints. Peak g is about 12 (margin 0.01 at 11.879), and it depends mainly on gamma, rising about 1.64 g/deg, with a weak D effect of about +0.375 g/m. Heatshield mass-fraction margin falls linearly with D at about 0.58 per m, reaching zero near D~3.385 at B=1.2, cone=69.5. Bondline temperature is far below its 450 K limit. Flux and temperature improve slightly with larger D, and the (B=1.2, cone=69.5) corner is the best of the points tested. The g limit puts the steep end near gamma ~ -3.57 at D 3.38. Shallower gamma lowers flux and raises T (about 24 kW/m2 and 11 K per deg). 17 of 60 evaluations returned no geometry. Failures are either a cone angle too small for the bluntness (B=1.2 with cone 66) or cd_fore hull extrapolation at cone 69-70 with B=1.25, or at D 3.0 to 2.8. I therefore stay near the known-good (B, cone) corner and make only three small probes.
evidence: C-8809880a095e (D3.38, gamma -3.5) has lower flux (273.5k) and lower T (391.86 K) than C-37807858716a (D3.34: 278.3k, 392.57 K). Larger D helps on both objectives, and its mass margin is only 0.0029.
Mass margin vs D at B=1.2, cone=69.5: 3.2 -> 0.1063, 3.3 -> 0.0496, 3.34 -> 0.0264, 3.36 -> 0.0147, 3.38 -> 0.0029. This gives a linear extrapolation to zero at D~3.385.
C-681765084fb2 (gamma -2.8) has 261k / 400.2 K, C-eabe3605e502 (gamma -3.2) has 270.9k / 395.7 K. Shallower gamma trades higher T for lower flux, so the front can be extended toward gamma -1.5.
C-f84c59a3cc23 (gamma -5.54) reaches T=378.9 K but g=15.6, so steeper entry is unreachable under the g limit.

Failures: C-40f2342796ee (D3.0, B1.2, cone 69), C-5b57439845df (B1.25, cone 70) and C-4b1b4e110042 (B1.25, cone 70) are hull-extrapolation failures. C-3cd51d4bc9fc (B1.2, cone 66) is an invalid geometry. Successful corner points are (1.2, 69.5), (1.15, 68.5), (1.1, 67) and (0.95, 69.5).
rounds.mechanism: Peak g depends mostly on entry angle, so it is nearly geometry-independent. The g limit therefore caps gamma near -3.57, and the mass fraction caps D near 3.385. Within those caps, larger D lowers ballistic coefficient, so flux and T fall. A larger nose radius (higher B) and a larger cone angle also lower flux and T slightly. The best design is at the corner D~3.38, B=1.2, cone~69.5, gamma just shallower than -3.57. Moving to that corner at each gamma should dominate the D3.34 front points. Shallower gamma at D=3.38 adds coverage of the low-flux, higher-T end. This is fitted from the data; the extrapolation to gamma of about -1.6 relies on smooth trends and is less certain.
rounds.uncertainty: The gamma-to-g edge is within about 0.01 g of the limit, so the -3.56 and -3.57 points may violate max_g. The mass margin at D=3.384 is about 0.0006, which is also marginal. The T(gamma) curve beyond gamma -2.8 is extrapolated and may be more convex than assumed. The B/cone probes (B 1.22, cone 70, cone 69.8) may hit cd_fore hull extrapolation failures, since the hull shape near the corner is unknown and (1.2, 69) failed at D3.0.

rounds.observation: All 16 front members lie on one curve: D=3.38, B=1.2, cone 69.5, varying only flight_path_angle. Three caps pin this corner. Peak g is 12.0 and depends almost only on gamma, with slope about 1.65 g/deg, so gamma stops near -3.57. The heatshield mass-fraction margin is only about 0.003 at D=3.38, which caps D near 3.385. B=1.2 and cone 69.5-70 are at the edge of the region the cd_fore surrogate covers. Seven of the eight recent geometry failures are extrapolation refusals or too-small-cone overlaps at high B or low cone. The extrapolation refusals are B=1.22, B=1.25, and the D=3.0, cone 69 point. Round 3 gained only 0.007 hypervolume, so the design is converged and further gains are small. What remains is (a) filling gaps along the gamma curve, (b) nudging D from 3.38 to 3.384 with cone 70, and (c) a few probes of B and cone sensitivity.
evidence: C-fc1968c6c49e (gamma -3.56): g=11.979, margin 0.0017. C-929cd2a6f018 (D=3.36, gamma -3.57): g=11.988, so g is nearly geometry-independent and the g limit is 12.0.
C-c39a84c0e158 (D=3.384, cone 69.5): mass margin 0.00056, against 0.0029 at D=3.38. That gives a slope of about 0.59 per m, so D is capped near 3.385. Flux is about 115k W/m2 lower per metre of D.

C-41b2ddb7397c (cone 70) has mass margin 0.0031, against 0.0029 at cone 69.5. Flux and T are essentially unchanged by cone (273480 vs about 273500 interpolated), so cone 70 buys slightly more D headroom at no cost.
C-1618bda1fac0 (D=3.2, B=1.0, cone 66) against C-94a9f7a46f9b (D=3.2, B=1.2, cone 69.5): lower B and cone raise flux by about 4% and T by about 1.5 K. That argues for B at its maximum.

C-68332aab55f2 (B=1.22), C-5b57439845df, C-4b1b4e110042 and C-40f2342796ee (D=3.0, cone 69) all failed on cd_fore extrapolation, so the safe region ends near B=1.2, cone 69.5-70. C-3cd51d4bc9fc (D=3.3, B=1.2, cone 66) is an invalid geometry.
The front's gamma spacing has gaps of 0.2-0.4 deg around -1.6..-2.0, -2.6..-3.0 and -3.3..-3.4. Flux runs from 229.7k to 275k and T from 416 K to 391 K along it.
rounds.mechanism: Stagnation heating scales roughly with Rn^-0.5 (prior knowledge, consistent with the flux-vs-B and flux-vs-D data). A larger D lowers the ballistic coefficient and raises nose radius, so both flux and T fall. A steeper gamma shortens the heat pulse and lowers T by about 10 K/deg, while raising g by about 1.65/deg. The optimum therefore sits at the corner: D at the mass-fraction cap, gamma at the g cap, and B and cone at the surrogate/geometry boundary. Reducing D relaxes g slightly (about 0.37 g per m) but raises T more than the steeper gamma removes it, so it does not help. Relative to the 450 K reference, T is the more valuable objective. The remaining gains are tiny gap-filling in gamma, a 0.004 m D increase using cone 70, and possibly a slightly higher B if the surrogate allows it.
rounds.uncertainty: The size of the B effect on mass fraction and on the hull boundary is unknown. The B=1.205 and B=1.21 probes may return a cd_fore extrapolation failure, which costs a slot. The D=3.384 designs have mass margin below 0.001, so a small model nonlinearity could push them infeasible. The g limit at gamma -3.565 has a margin of about 0.001, and my estimates of the D and B effects on g are extrapolated from few points. Flux and T predictions for the lower-B and lower-D probes are extrapolated from single points at different gamma.

The remaining lever is the position along gamma. Given the corner is saturated, the reliable gain is to densify the front, since hypervolume is a staircase and each intermediate point adds a small area. I do this at the proven mass-safe D=3.384.
