rounds.observation: The feasible front is one line of designs at D~3.384, B=1.2, cone=70, spread over gamma from -1.5 to -3.567. Flux runs 227k to 275k W/m2 and bondline T runs 418 to 391 K. The front is pinned at three limits: D by heatshield mass fraction (margin ~0 at D=3.385), gamma by max_g (margin 0.0005 at -3.567), and B and cone by the surrogate hull and the variable bound. Eight of the ten geometry failures came from trying B>1.2, so B=1.2 is the practical ceiling. Hypervolume gains have shrunk to about 0.0003 per round, so the front is near saturation. The fixed 2.5e6 flux reference means a real hypervolume gain would need lower T at similar flux, and I found no lever for that in the data.
evidence: C-78a9a956afab (gamma -3.567) has max_g margin 0.0005 and mass margin 0.00014. C-733cdcb996ae (D=3.385) has mass margin 0.00014 against 0.00074 at D=3.384, so the D cap is about 3.3852.

C-1618bda1fac0 (D=3.2, gamma -3.7, g=12.139) and C-94a9f7a46f9b (D=3.2, gamma -3.8, g=12.309) sit about 0.07 below the D=3.384 g-vs-gamma line. So g falls only ~0.4 per metre of D, which lets gamma steepen by only ~0.24 deg per metre. Meanwhile flux and T rise strongly as D falls (C-94a9f7a46f9b: 304k W/m2 and 392.2 K, worse than the corner), so shrinking D does not pay.

Along the D=3.384 line, T falls about 10-13 K/deg of steepening and flux rises about 24k W/m2/deg (e.g. C-6a031c8b7ef2 to C-78a9a956afab). Both are nearly linear, so interpolated gamma values are predictable.

C-0202524b57fd, C-1d24bfa5f84e, C-5b57439845df, C-4b1b4e110042, C-68332aab55f2, C-3d41ce848a30 and C-05beb8f06d5f all failed the cd_fore convex-hull check. That confirms B>1.2 is unreachable; the sixth failure, C-3cd51d4bc9fc, is a cone-angle geometry failure. So I keep B<=1.2 and cone=70.

rounds.mechanism: Peak g depends almost entirely on gamma, with a weak D dependence, which caps gamma near -3.57. Flux and T fall as D, B and cone rise, because ballistic coefficient drops and nose radius grows. That pushes D, B and cone to their caps (mass fraction, hull, bound). This is my physical reading of the data, partly informed by the general Rn^-0.5 stagnation-heating scaling from prior knowledge. Little hypervolume is left, so I spend most of the slots on gamma values not yet evaluated, including gaps in the front where flux steps by 3-5k. I also push gamma and D to the g and mass limits, and add two low-cost probes: one near the mass cap and one on the D-g tradeoff.
rounds.uncertainty: The main risk is duplicates of the 19 front points I cannot see; I used non-round gamma values to reduce that. Interpolated T and flux should be good to about 0.1 K and 0.3k W/m2. The limit-pushing points (gamma near -3.57, D near 3.3852) may cross g or mass-fraction margins of ~1e-4. The B=1.19 and D=3.3 probes rely on extrapolating the mass-fraction and g dependence on D and B from only a few points.

rounds.observation: The feasible front is essentially one line: D=3.384-3.385, B=1.2, cone=70 (all at their caps), with flight path angle gamma swept from -1.5 to -3.57. Peak g reaches 12 at gamma near -3.57. Heatshield mass fraction caps D near 3.3853, and the cd_fore surrogate hull caps B near 1.2. Normalised hypervolume has stalled at about 0.3555 over rounds 4-6 (gains of 1e-3, 3e-4, 2e-4). Because the flux reference is 2.5e6 and front fluxes are 227k-275k, hypervolume is driven almost entirely by bondline temperature. Fine spacing along gamma and the corner point matter more than any other region.
evidence: C-d091f610d31f (D 3.385, gamma -3.5695): flux 274560, T 391.09, g margin 1.3e-4, mass-fraction margin 1.4e-4. This is the corner design, pinned by g and mass fraction.
C-c3f9f333f061 and C-9690b44cafcb: mass-fraction margin goes 8.6e-5 to 2.7e-5 as D goes 3.3851 to 3.3852, so the D cap is about 3.38525.
C-3da7d9bac3e7 and C-eed229743768: g rises about 1.6-1.7 per deg near -3.5, and T falls about 10 K/deg.
C-363a563b3536 (D 3.3): flux 285110, T 392.49 against 274.5k and 391.1 at D 3.385. Smaller D is worse in both objectives.
C-94a9f7a46f9b and C-1618bda1fac0: g is close to independent of B and cone, and rises only about 0.4 per metre of D. Stepping to smaller D therefore buys almost no extra gamma.

C-0202524b57fd, C-5b57439845df, C-3d41ce848a30 and C-05beb8f06d5f: B above 1.2 at cone 70 falls outside the surrogate hull. C-3cd51d4bc9fc: cone 66 with B 1.2 is invalid geometry. Both are cap-like limits.

rounds.mechanism: Peak g depends almost entirely on gamma (about 1.65 per deg near -3.57, less at shallow angles). That sets a fixed steepness cap, which in turn sets the minimum T reachable. Larger D lowers ballistic coefficient and raises nose radius, so flux and T both fall, but the mass-fraction limit stops D at about 3.385. Higher B and cone have the same helpful effect and sit at the hull and variable bounds. Mass fraction scales roughly as D squared and worsens slightly as cone or B drop. The optimum is therefore a fixed corner. Remaining improvement is limited to filling gamma gaps on the line, nudging gamma to the g cap, and a few probes of cone and B near the corner. This is based on the data; the Rn^-0.5 stagnation scaling is prior knowledge and was not needed for these picks.
rounds.uncertainty: Line-interpolated predictions are reliable to a few hundred W/m2 and a few tenths of a K. The corner points (gamma -3.5700) sit within about 1e-4 of the g and mass-fraction limits, so a feasibility flip is possible. The cone and B probes could trigger a geometry or hull failure, since the boundary between cone 66 (invalid) and cone 69.5 (valid) is unknown. The cone and B sensitivities are only weakly identified from confounded rows. I do not expect any hidden basin, but I cannot rule one out in unexplored corners.

rounds.mechanism: Flux and T fall with ballistic coefficient and nose radius, which favours large D, B and cone. The mass fraction (~D^2, slightly worse at lower B) caps D. Peak g depends almost only on gamma and caps steepness. This is my reading of the data, plus the general Rn^-0.5 heating scaling from prior knowledge. rounds.observation: The feasible front is essentially a one-parameter curve in flight_path_angle. Every non-dominated point sits at D~3.385, B=1.2, cone=70 (flux 227k to 275k W/m2, bondline T 418 to 391 K). Three limits pin the corner. Mass fraction caps D (margin 2.7e-5 at D=3.3852). The surrogate hull blocks B>1.2 (seven hull failures near this corner). The cone is at its variable bound of 70. Peak g caps steepness at about -3.5702 (margin 1.3e-5). Round 8 gained only 4.5e-5 hypervolume, so almost nothing is left. The remaining options are a marginally larger D and denser gamma coverage.

rounds.mechanism: Flux and T fall as ballistic coefficient falls and nose radius rises, which favours large D, high B and large cone, all at their caps. Steeper entry lowers T by about 10 K/deg and raises flux by about 22k W/m2 per deg, while raising peak g by about 1.66 per deg. The g limit therefore fixes the steep end, and the front is the gamma sweep from -1.5 to -3.57. Two improvements remain. Pushing D from 3.3852 to 3.38523 uses up the mass-fraction slack, a tiny gain in flux and T. Filling gaps in the gamma sweep at that D trims the step-like hypervolume loss between neighbouring points. This relies on the Rn^-0.5 heating scaling from prior knowledge as well as on the data.
rounds.uncertainty: The mass-fraction zero-crossing (~3.385245) is extrapolated linearly from two points, so D=3.38523 keeps only about 1e-5 of margin. The g margin at gamma=-3.57025 is very thin, and the small D increase adds roughly 1e-5 g. Expected gains are of order 1e-5 in hypervolume. Predictions are interpolated from neighbouring rows and may be off by a few hundred W/m2 and a few tenths of a K.

rounds.observation: Only 2 of 20 evaluated designs are feasible, and only C-ca305253716b is non-dominated (flux 345120 W/m2, Tbond 406.56 K). Eleven of the 20 failed on geometry, so the hypervolume is mostly limited by wasted slots and by the max_g limit (12 g), which caps how steep the entry angle can be. I backed out the constraint limits from the margins: max_g 12, bondline 450 K, and heatshield mass fraction roughly 0.09*D^2 relative to its limit, so D is capped near 3.3 m. The geometry failures are consistent with nose radius = bluntness*D and shoulder radius = 0.1*D. Fore-cone length is then proportional to 0.4 - (b-0.1)*cos(theta), so a design is valid only if (b-0.1)*cos(theta) < 0.4. The formula reproduces the reported negative lengths for C-892b8b20e709 and C-c170e00795a8. I keep it below about 0.38 in every proposal. Bluntness above 0.9 needs a cone half-angle of 60 deg or more.
evidence: Geometry: C-c170e00795a8 (b=0.929, 53.06 deg gives 0.4985), C-892b8b20e709 (0.608) and C-77238b231f4a fail. C-ca305253716b (0.367), C-30ab3c9fdbef (0.362) and C-f1dfaff79f31 (0.246) are valid, consistent with a 0.4 threshold.

max_g: 9.85 at gamma=-2.32 (C-30ab3c9fdbef), 11.20 at -3.16 (C-ca305253716b), 13.57 at -4.54 (C-7e930f570744). This fits g ~ 6.1 + 1.63*|gamma| for large D, so the g limit of 12 allows |gamma| up to about 3.6 deg. Small-D designs (C-7139ecfe995b, C-6c8d751b6b54) run 1-1.5 g higher.
Mass fraction: margins of 0.185 (D=3.007), 0.171 (D=3.044), 0.452 (D=2.48), -0.37 (D=3.74) and -0.77 (D=4.33) scale as D^2. Zero margin falls near D~3.3-3.35 m.

Scaling fitted to the rows: flux falls with D and with nose radius, and rises only weakly with |gamma| (C-7e930f570744 vs C-ca305253716b, C-1d847642b793). Bondline temperature (T-300) scales roughly as D^-0.5 * sin(gamma)^-0.35 with almost no dependence on nose radius, so steeper entry lowers T (C-1d847642b793 372 K, C-0a0993b4b67b 374 K). Larger bluntness at high cone angle therefore lowers flux without raising T.

Small-D designs (C-6c8d751b6b54: 2.63e6 W/m2, 510 K; C-7139ecfe995b) are far worse on both objectives and infeasible, so the useful region is D ~3.0-3.35 m, gamma ~ -3.3 to -3.6 deg, with high bluntness and cone angle.
rounds.mechanism: Bigger diameter lowers ballistic coefficient, so peak density and heat load fall. A larger nose radius (bluntness*D) cuts stagnation-point flux roughly as 1/sqrt(Rn). Steeper entry shortens the heating pulse and lowers the integrated load that drives bondline temperature, but raises peak deceleration, which max_g caps near gamma ~ -3.6 deg. Large cone angle raises drag and gives room for high bluntness within the geometry limit. Heatshield mass fraction grows with D^2 and is the binding constraint at the large-D end. Tbond has the larger effect on hypervolume, since each 10 K is worth about 0.067 of the normalised T axis, so I push toward the steepest gamma that keeps g under 12, the largest allowed D, and high bluntness. Some proposals probe the g and mass-fraction boundaries and single-variable effects (bluntness, cone angle, gamma) to calibrate the model.
rounds.uncertainty: The scaling exponents and the g and mass-fraction fits come from 9 valid points, so the numeric predictions are rough (about +/-10% on flux, +/-5 K on T). Geometry validity assumes Rn=b*D and Rs=0.1*D, fitted to two failure lengths, and there may be other minimum-length rules. I do not know how cone angle enters drag, g or mass fraction, and proposals at D>=3.3 or gamma <= -3.55 may fail max_g or mass fraction.

rounds.observation: None of the 20 evaluated designs is feasible, so there is no front yet. 10 of 20 returned no geometry. Every one of those has a cone half-angle too small for its bluntness. Fitting the 10 failures and the valid rows gives a validity rule: with nose radius = bluntness*D and shoulder radius = 0.1*D, the fore cone has positive length only if cos(theta) < 0.4/(bluntness-0.1). That means bluntness <= 0.5 is always valid, bluntness 0.7 needs theta > 48 deg, 0.9 needs > 60 deg, 1.1 needs > 66.4 deg, and 1.2 needs > 68.7 deg. The rule reproduces the sign of the fore-cone length in all 10 failures and every valid row. The constraint limits back-computed from the margins are max_g <= 12.0 and bondline T <= 450 K. Peak g depends mostly on |gamma| (about 6.3*sqrt|gamma| for D > 2.5), so gamma must be shallower than about -3.5 deg. The mass-fraction limit is not stated. Its value scales roughly as D^2 times a coefficient that falls with cone angle (about 0.089 at theta >= 62 deg, about 0.11 at theta <= 40 deg). That puts the D limit near 3.0-3.3 m. In these data, bondline T falls as D, nose radius and steepness rise. Peak flux falls with larger nose radius and larger D. Because T spans only 300-450 K against a 2.5e6 flux reference, reducing T is worth far more hypervolume, so I favour large D, large bluntness and gamma near -3.3 to -3.5, with a few shallower points to spread the front.
evidence: Geometry failures C-0e7ec9742f84 (b=.94, th=55.1), C-2e989122c857 (b=.97, th=59.8), C-7fd3f4505944 (b=.75, th=36.4) and C-de1dd6ca3952 (b=.84, th=40.6) all violate cos(th) < 0.4/(b-0.1). Valid rows C-36f9165b9496 (b=.87, th=65) and C-26bc5a06b4e4 (b=.70, th=51.6) satisfy it.

max_g margins imply a 12.0 limit: C-ee99f55de428 has 10.189 with margin 0.1509. Bondline margin gives 450 K: 455.54 with margin -0.01232. g vs gamma: C-f97dae207371 (-1.85 deg) 9.42, C-ee99f55de428 (-2.64) 10.19, C-63aaa0985529 (-4.10) 12.49, C-36f9165b9496 (-4.86) 13.8.

Mass fraction is roughly proportional to D^2. C-63aaa0985529 (D=2.99) is at 0.97 of the limit, C-ab9827dc6929 (D=3.21) at 1.004, C-baa2f9e65f32 (D=4.01) at 1.47, C-50a0a474d0f6 (D=1.23) at 0.15. High-theta rows (C-36f9165b9496, C-12010dd082dd, C-c72c38c9187a) sit near 0.089 of the limit per m^2, against about 0.11 for C-f97dae207371 and C-63aaa0985529 at theta <= 38 deg.

Peak flux fits q ~ 7e6*sqrt(sin(gamma)/(D^2*Rn)) within about 10%, where Rn = b*D. Bondline T-300 fits about 0.307*sqrt(q/|gamma_deg|). For example C-ab9827dc6929 (q=479k, gamma -4.26) gives 335*0.307 = 103 K against 103.1 K observed, and C-63aaa0985529 gives 108.8 K against 109.6 K.

C-63aaa0985529 (D=2.985, gamma=-4.1) has T=409.6 K and q=515k, and misses only on max_g (-0.04). C-ab9827dc6929 misses on max_g and mass fraction. Together they show the feasible region needs D of about 3.0 or less and |gamma| of about 3.5 or less.
rounds.mechanism: Peak deceleration in a ballistic entry is set mainly by entry angle. That makes max_g a ceiling on |gamma|, and the ceiling is where bondline temperature is lowest (T scales roughly as gamma^-0.25). Heat-shield mass fraction scales with the shield area, about D^2. It is lower for wide cones because they have less lateral area, which caps D near 3.0-3.3 m. Within those two limits, a large nose radius (Rn = b*D) lowers stagnation heat flux and heat load together. So the best trade-off has D near its mass limit, high bluntness with a cone angle above the validity boundary, and gamma just inside the g limit. Shallower gamma trades a little T for lower peak flux, which extends the front.
rounds.uncertainty: The g estimate for gamma near -3.5 (about 11.8 against a limit of 12) has only about 3% margin. I have no data on how theta and D affect g. The dependence of mass fraction on theta is inferred from correlation, not isolated. The validity rule is fitted; the length discrepancy (about 2%) suggests the shoulder radius or nose definition is slightly off, so I keep at least 1.3 deg of margin on theta. Flux and T models are rough fits (10-15% error) and small-D rows deviate. I do not know whether very high bluntness or theta near 70 deg adds flux penalties (e.g. shoulder heating) that this reduced-order model may include. Prior knowledge (Allen-Eggers scaling) supports the g and T trends, but the numeric fits come from the 10 valid rows.

rounds.observation: The feasible front has one point, C-05ff421c45e2 (279k W/m2, 394.04 K). The normalised hypervolume of 0.331 matches that point exactly. The temperature axis dominates the score, because 1 K is worth roughly 15 times more than 10k W/m2. The feasible region is a narrow cluster near D 3.0-3.37 m, bluntness 1.0-1.25, cone 66-70 deg and gamma -3.1 to -3.6 deg. Three constraints bound it. max_g <= 12 sets a steepest gamma of about -3.58 deg. Heatshield mass fraction caps D at about 3.38 m at high bluntness and cone angle. Geometry validity caps bluntness at about 0.4/cos(cone)+0.1, which is 1.27 at 70 deg. Steeper gamma, larger D and higher bluntness all lower both objectives, so the best remaining move is to push toward the corner where all three limits meet.
evidence: C-3583b7488cf2 (D3.3, bl1.2, c70, gamma -3.6) has the lowest temperature of any near-feasible candidate at 392.29 K and 285.6k, but g=12.016 fails the limit by 0.1%. C-dcc8aaeb364a (gamma -3.55) gives g=11.921, so the g limit sits near gamma -3.58 to -3.59.

C-05ff421c45e2 (D3.35, bl1.1) has mass margin 0.0179. C-0d18a7fb8799 (D3.3, bl1.15) has 0.048, C-15107d6a0298 (D3.2, bl1.2) has 0.106 and C-613443d901da (D3.0069) has 0.209. Margin falls about 0.6 per metre of D, so D is capped near 3.37-3.38.

C-3a694f0320f1 and C-dcc8aaeb364a differ only in gamma (-3.4 vs -3.55). Mass margin is identical at 0.04787, so mass fraction does not depend on gamma. Temperature falls about 1.1 K per 0.1 deg of steeper gamma. Flux rises only about 2.8k per 0.1 deg.

Geometry failures such as C-892b8b20e709 and C-a91d9ef63c92 fit an axial cone length of (0.4 + 0.1cos(theta) - bl*cos(theta))*D / tan(theta). I checked this against the failure messages (-369 vs -367 mm, -2983 vs -2984 mm). bl=1.24 at cone 70 is valid, with a positive length of about 12 mm.
Flux falls with bluntness and D. C-3583b7488cf2 (bl1.2, D3.3) and C-0d18a7fb8799 (bl1.15) show about -3k per +0.05 bl. C-05ff421c45e2 (D3.35) has the lowest flux at 279k.
rounds.mechanism: Peak deceleration in a ballistic entry is roughly independent of ballistic coefficient, so max_g is set mainly by gamma (my prior knowledge, consistent with the g values in the table). That makes about -3.58 deg the steepest allowed entry. Steeper entry shortens the heat pulse and lowers bondline temperature. A larger diameter lowers ballistic coefficient and raises the nose radius, which cuts flux and temperature, but heatshield mass fraction limits D. Higher bluntness and cone angle reduce flux and slightly help mass margin. The best corner is therefore D about 3.30-3.37, bluntness 1.24-1.25, cone 70 deg and gamma about -3.55 to -3.58. I also add a few shallow-gamma, low-flux points to spread the front along the flux axis.
rounds.uncertainty: The g-limit is close to the gamma range I probe, so several proposals with gamma between -3.55 and -3.585 could fail max_g by 0.1-0.5%. Mass margin at D 3.36-3.37 is predicted to be only about 0.01 and could turn negative. My sensitivities are rough finite differences from confounded rows. The geometry-validity rule is fitted to only two failures, and bl 1.25 at cone 70 leaves only about 8 mm of fore-cone length. Predicted temperature gains are small (1-3 K).

rounds.observation: The feasible front is a tight cluster at D≈3.0-3.3 m, bluntness 1.0-1.2, cone 68-70°, gamma -2 to -3.5°, with flux 283-300 kW/m² and bondline T 396-419 K. Hypervolume is about 0.32, and it is limited mainly by T: the normalised T axis (300-450 K) has far more room than the flux axis (reference 2.5 MW/m²). From the data I fitted rough local trends: T falls about 17 K per metre of D, about 0.8 K per 0.1 of bluntness, and about 11.7 K per degree of steepening gamma. Flux falls roughly as D^-1.45 and drops about 8%/deg with shallower gamma. max_g depends almost only on gamma (about 11.83 at gamma -3.5, D 3.25), so the limit of 12 caps gamma near -3.58. Heatshield mass fraction scales as D², with 1-margin ≈ 0.79*(D/3)², so D is capped near 3.37 m. Cone angle affects T, flux and g very little but is best at 70°. All 8 geometry failures have cone angle too small for the bluntness, which suggests a bluntness limit that shrinks as the cone gets shallower. This is an inference, not verified.
evidence: C-19d65f7d82f4 (D3.25, bl1.0, c69, g-3.5): T 395.58 and flux 300k with mass margin 0.072. C-bd65eb0949c1 (D3.3, g-3.3): margin 0.042. Mass margin therefore hits zero near D≈3.37.

C-29603553ab30 (g-2.0): flux 283k, T 418.8. C-aa9546beae98 (g-2.4): T 414.5. C-ec050d7f0c55 (g-3.5): T 401.4 at D3.0. So T drops about 11-12 K per degree of steepening, at the cost of higher flux and g.
max_g at g-3.5 is 11.61 (D2.7), 11.74 (D3.0) and 11.83 (D3.25), while cone 62/66/70 at D3.0 give identical g (C-7e855dcecd98, C-ec050d7f0c55, C-5eac89a9568b). g is set by gamma, with a weak D effect.
Higher bluntness lowers both objectives slightly: C-268997241f64 (bl1.2, D3.1, g-3.4) has flux 307k and T 398.1, versus C-31cee390321b (bl1.1, c69.5) at 312.6k and 398.8.

Infeasible steep-entry points (C-36f9165b9496, C-ab9827dc6929) gain little T (T≈398-403) but break max_g. Small-D points have high flux. The high-D, high-bluntness corner is therefore the best region.

All 8 geometry failures have a small cone angle for their bluntness, e.g. C-2e989122c857 (bl0.97, c59.8) and C-7fd3f4505944 (bl0.75, c36). Every point with c≥62 and bl≤1.2 was valid, so I keep c=70 with bl≤1.25.
rounds.mechanism: Bondline T is driven by the heat pulse. A larger D lowers the ballistic coefficient, so peak heating occurs higher in the atmosphere and is lower. A steeper gamma shortens the pulse but raises g. The g limit of 12 fixes gamma at about -3.55, and the mass-fraction limit fixes D at about 3.35-3.37. A larger nose radius (bluntness) and a high cone angle reduce stagnation flux without changing g. The optimum T is therefore at the corner D≈3.35, bl 1.2, c70, gamma≈-3.5, near about 392 K and 279 kW/m². Since flux is cheap in hypervolume terms, I also spread points along the front with shallower gamma at D≈3.35 (lower flux, higher T) to cover the trade-off.
rounds.uncertainty: All numbers are extrapolations from local trends. D≥3.36 could violate mass fraction if my scaling is off, and gamma≤-3.55 could violate g at large D. Bluntness 1.25 at c70 is beyond the tested range and could be an invalid geometry. Shallow-gamma flux and T predictions rely on interpolation between D3.0 data and the fitted D scaling.

rounds.observation: Round 2 lost 18 of 20 evaluations to 'aero surface extrapolation' failures. Every failure has bluntness >= 1.24 at cone 70, plus (1.2, cone 69). All the successful high-bluntness points sit at cone 70 with bluntness <= 1.2, or at (1.12, cone 68). The valid region for the cd_fore surrogate therefore ends at bluntness ~1.2 on the cone=70 edge, and inside that the edge runs roughly from (1.12, 68) to (1.2, 70). The feasible front is only 3 points, clustered at ~280-290 kW/m2 and ~393-394 K. Bondline temperature has the larger hypervolume leverage: 1 K is worth about as much as ~40 kW/m2 of flux. The binding constraints are max_g (limit 12, near gamma ~ -3.58) and heatshield mass fraction (limit reached near D ~3.38). The nearly feasible C-3583b7488cf2 (b=1.2, cone 70, gamma -3.6) has the lowest temperature (392.3 K) and fails max_g by only 0.13%.
evidence: C-3583b7488cf2: b=1.2, cone 70, D=3.3, gamma -3.6 gives 285.6 kW/m2, 392.29 K, g=12.016, so it is infeasible by 0.13%. Gamma -3.58 should be just feasible.
g rises about 1.7 g/deg of steepening: C-05ff421c45e2 (gamma -3.4) gives 11.70 g and C-b57da803fe39 (gamma -3.55) gives 11.95 g. That puts the g limit near gamma -3.58 to -3.59.

Mass-fraction margin falls as D grows: D=3.3 gives 0.046-0.050 (C-bd537396e7e1, C-3583b7488cf2), D=3.35 gives 0.015-0.018 (C-05ff421c45e2, C-b57da803fe39), and D=3.74 gives -0.37 (C-0a0993b4b67b). That is about 0.6-0.9 per metre, so D <= ~3.37 is needed.
Every one of the 18 round-2 failures (e.g. C-ec5c054f9438, C-460ff98d4dde) has b>=1.24, or b=1.2 with cone 69. These are all outside the hull, while C-3583b7488cf2 (1.2, cone 70) is valid.

Shallower gamma lowers flux and raises temperature: C-05ff421c45e2 (-3.4) has 279k and 394.0 K, versus C-b57da803fe39 (-3.55) at 288.5k and 393.2 K. This supports a few shallow-gamma points to spread the front.
rounds.mechanism: Peak flux scales roughly as sqrt(rho_peak/Rn), with rho_peak proportional to ballistic coefficient times sin(gamma). Flux therefore falls with a larger D (about D^-1.5), with a larger nose radius (higher bluntness), and with a shallower gamma. Bondline temperature follows the integrated heat load. Steeper entry shortens the pulse and lowers temperature, until the max_g cap is hit at about -3.58 deg. Maximum cone angle (70) and bluntness of about 1.2 minimise both objectives, and D is pushed to the mass-fraction limit near 3.36-3.38. I stay strictly inside the known-valid bluntness/cone region (cone 70 with b<=1.2, plus a few interior points). I probe b=1.22 once to locate the hull edge. A handful of shallow-gamma points at b=1.2 extend the front toward low flux. Flux and temperature predictions come from a simple scaling anchored on C-3583b7488cf2, which is prior-knowledge physics, not a fit.
rounds.uncertainty: The exact hull boundary between b=1.2 and b=1.24 at cone 70 is unknown, so the b=1.22 probe may fail. The g margin near gamma -3.58 is about 0.2% and depends slightly on b and D, so some steep-gamma points may narrowly fail. The mass-fraction margin at D >= 3.37 is extrapolated from few points and may depend on gamma through heat load. The temperature rise at very shallow gamma (-2 to -3) is extrapolated with high uncertainty.

rounds.observation: All 10 feasible non-dominated points sit on one curve: D about 3.35 m, bluntness 1.2, cone 70 deg (the upper bound), with only flight-path angle varied. Along it, gamma trades heat flux (231k to 278k W/m2) against bondline T (418.7 K to 391.9 K). The binding limits are max_g (about 12, which sets gamma near -3.55) and heatshield_mass_fraction (which sets D near 3.38 at cone 70). Flux is already about 0.1 of the 2.5M reference, so hypervolume gains come almost entirely from lowering T, and only marginally from lowering flux. The local optimum is close, so I mostly refine along its active constraints.
evidence: C-04a14692e856 (gamma -1.5) to C-b460a0993d3f (gamma -3.55): T falls 418.67 to 391.89 K, flux rises 230.7k to 278.3k, and max_g margin falls 0.232 to 0.004.

rounds.mechanism: Peak g in a ballistic entry is set mainly by gamma, so the g limit of 12 caps |gamma| near 3.56. Mass fraction grows roughly with D^2 and falls slightly with higher cone angle and bluntness, so D is capped near 3.38 at cone 70. High bluntness and cone 70 give high drag, low flux and low T. Because max_g margin is nearly independent of D and cone, the best design pushes D to the mass limit and gamma to the g limit, and the rest of the front is a gamma sweep at that D. All quantitative predictions come from linear fits to the tabulated rows (the D slopes above and the gamma slopes along the D=3.35 line), not from an independent model.

The optimum therefore sits where the mass-fraction limit (D about 3.385) and the g limit (gamma about -3.57) meet, at the highest bluntness and cone angle the surrogate hull allows. rounds.mechanism: Bondline T is set by heat-pulse severity: it falls with lower ballistic coefficient (larger D, higher-Cd blunt 70° cone) and with steeper entry. g and mass fraction cap gamma and D, and the corner (1.2, 70) maximises Cd and minimises shield mass.
